label: bedding-plane cave
description: A cavity developed along a bedding-plane and elongate in cross-section as a result.

label: cave system
description: A collection of caves interconnected by enterable passages or linked hydrologically or a cave with an extensive complex of chambers and passages.

label: spring
description: Springs are typically where an aquifer surface meets the ground surface or where there is a fissure.
A surface landform which provides an egress for groundwater or steam to flow out of the ground.

label: dead cave
description: A cave without streams or drips of water.

label: wadi
description: The temporality of wadis is problematic in deciding whether they are watercourses or valleys.
A valley or ravine, bounded by relatively steep banks, which in the rainy season becomes a watercourse.

label: ditch
description: A small, human-made channel which has been dug for draining or irrigating the land.

label: geyser
description: A hot spring that erupts periodically, ejecting a column of hot water and steam into the air.

label: hot spring
description: A spring through which groundwater, heated by geothermal energy, flows.

label: man-made tunnel
description: A tunnel constructed by human means.

label: cave
description: Naturally formed, subterranean open area or chamber.

label: tunnel
description: An underground or underwater passage.

label: fault cave
description: A cave developed along a fault or fault zone, either by movement of the fault or by preferential solution along it.

label: mountain
description: A mountain is generally steeper than a hill, but there is no universally accepted standard definition for the height of a mountain or a hill although a mountain usually has an identifiable summit. The USGS had previously defined mountains as localised elevations of more than 300 meters; however, the organisation has accepted there are no technical definitions in the US. In ENVO, we primarily use the UNEP-WCMC classification to be compliant with SDG monitoring, but we can host other classifications on request: http://www.fao.org/sustainable-development-goals/indicators/1542/en/
A landform that extends above the surrounding terrain in a limited area.

label: hill
description: A rounded elevation of limited extent rising above the surrounding land with local relief of less than 300m.

label: mountain pass
description: A lower point that allows easier access through a mountain range. A pass has the general form of a saddle between two mountains.

label: plain
description: A region of general uniform slope, comparatively level, and of considerable extent.

label: cliff
description: A slope which is part of a rocky elevation and which has a high degree of steepness.

label: sea cliff
description: A cliff that is a margin of a sea or ocean.

label: inland cliff
description: A cliff which is not adjacent to a major water body.

label: coastal plain
description: An area of flat, low-lying land adjacent to a coast and separated from the interior by other features.

label: beach
description: A landform consisting of loose rock particles such as sand, gravel, shingle, pebbles, cobble, or even shell fragments along the shoreline of a body of water.

label: sea beach
description: A beach which is part of a sea shore.

label: lacustrine beach
description: A beach which is part of a lake shore.

label: volcanic feature
description: A part of an astronomical body associated with a volcano - an opening, or rupture, in that body's surface or crust - which allows hot, molten rock, ash and gases to escape from deep below the surface.

label: caldera
description: A feature formed by the collapse of land following a volcanic eruption.

label: valley
description: Valleys are typically located between hills our mountains.
A depression which has been formed as a result of erosion by water or ice and which is low-lying, bordered by higher ground, and especially elongate.

label: lava tunnel
description: These are usually classified as a sub-type of volcanic cave, rather than a tunnel.
A tunnel formed by the flow of molten lava, which has subsequently drained out.

label: artificial channel
description: A channel of a watercource which has been constructed by humans or their technologies.

label: mineral spring
description: A spring which  water contains a significant amount of dissolved minerals, that derive from the rocks through which the water flows.

label: sulfur spring
description: A spring through which water with elevated levels of dissolved derivatives of sulfur flows.

label: badland
description: An arid terrain with clay-rich soil that has been extensively eroded by wind and water.

label: dry valley
description: Typically found in either Karst (limestone) or chalk terrain.

label: stream valley
description: A valley that contains, and has been formed by, a stream.

label: irrigation ditch
description: A ditch that supplies water to surrounding land.

label: drainage ditch
description: A ditch that collects water from the surrounding land.

label: bank
description: The sloping margin of a watercourse, serving to confine it to its natural channel.

label: stream bank
description: The sloping margin of a stream, serving to confine it to its natural channel.

label: river bank
description: The sloping margin of a river, serving to confine it to its natural channel.

label: cirque
description: A depression which is semicircular or crescent-shaped, found towards the crest of a mountain, and formed by the erosional processes caused by the motion of a glacier.

label: peat cut
description: An artificial working of peatland to remove the peat.

label: canyon
description: Relatively narrow, deep depression with steep sides, the bottom of which generally has a continuous slope.

label: dune
description: A hill of sand built by eolian processes.

label: river valley
description: A valley that contains, and has been formed by, a river.

label: isthmus
description: Narrow section of land in a body of water connecting two larger land areas.

label: karst
description: Karsts usually form in masses of carbonate rock such as limestone or dolomite. Karst landscapes display distinctive surface features and underground drainages, and in some examples there may be little or no surface drainage.

label: elevated landform
description: A landform elevated above the surrounding area.

label: moraine
description: An accumulation of boulders, stones, or other debris carried and deposited by a glacier.

label: levee
description: An artificial slope or wall, usually earthen, which parallels the course of a river, built for the purpose of containing the river.

label: mesa
description: An elevated area of land with a flat top and sides that are usually steep cliffs. Mesas form in areas where horizontally layered rocks are uplifted by tectonic activity.

label: mound
description: A rounded elevated area.

label: nunatak
description: "peak" in the definition is understood as a synonym of mount, rather than of summit. Nunataks may also refer to areas of ridges. The definition and placement of this class may need to be revised.
The exposed summit of a ridge, mountain, or peak not covered with ice or snow within an ice field or glacier. The term is typically used in areas where a permanent ice mass is present.

label: plateau
description: An elevated and comparatively level expanse of land.

label: hanging valley
description: A tributary valley with the floor at a higher relief than the main channel into which it flows. They are most commonly associated with U-shaped valleys when a tributary glacier flows into a glacier of larger volume.

label: sinkhole
description: A natural depression or hole in the surface topography caused by the removal of soil or bedrock, often both, by water. Sinkholes may vary in size from less than a meter to several hundred meters both in diameter and depth, and vary in form from soil-lined bowls to bedrock-edged chasms.

label: ephemeral spring
description: A spring through which fluid intermittently flows.

label: permanent spring
description: A spring whose flow is continuous.

label: hydrothermal vent
description: A fissure in the Earths's surface from which geothermally heated water issues.

label: black smoker
description: A hydrothermal vent found on the ocean floor. The vents are formed in fields hundreds of meters wide when superheated water from below the Earth's crust comes through the ocean floor. The superheated water is rich in dissolved minerals from the crust, most notably sulfides, which crystallize to create a chimney-like structure around each vent. When the superheated water in the vent comes in contact with the cold ocean water, many minerals are precipitated, creating the distinctive black color. The metal sulfides that are deposited can become massive sulfide ore deposits in time.

label: continental shelf
description: The continental shelf is a gentle slope. This class refers to the geographical continental shelf and not the legal concept of the same name.

A slope which a) extends the perimeter of a continent, b) is covered by a shallow marine water body during interglacial periods, c) has a low degree of steepness relative to a continental slope or rise.

label: abyssal plain
description: A flat or very gently sloping areas of the deep ocean basin floor.

label: maar
description: A broad, low relief crater that results from a phreatic eruption or explosion caused by groundwater contact with hot lava or magma. The maar typically fills with water to form a relatively shallow crater lake.

label: volcanic crater
description: A crater formed by a volcano, within which occurs a vent (or vents) from which magma erupts as gases, lava, and ejecta.

label: glacial valley
description: A valley that contains, or contained, a glacier and was formed by glacial activity. Typically U-shaped in cross-section.

label: lateral moraine
description: The parallel ridges of till deposited along the sides of an alglacier. The unconsolidated debris is deposited on top of the glacier by frost shattering of the valley walls and from tributary streams flowing into the valley. The till is carried along the glacial margin until the glacier melts.

label: medial moraine
description: A moriane formed when the inside lateral moraines of two glaciers merge together. They form a ridge down the center of the combined glaciers.

label: ground moraine
description: A till covered area with irregular topography and no ridges, often forming gently rolling hills or plains. Forms by the accumulation of till under the ice by lodgement, but may also be deposited as the glacier retreats.

label: terminal moraine
description: Ridges of unconsolidated debris deposited at the snout or end of the glacier. They usually reflect the shape of the glacier's terminus.

label: scroll plane
description: A plain where a stream meanders across an area with a very low gradient, usually with a fairly continuous discharge. In addition to meanders, scroll plains are also characterised by many oxbow lakes.

label: till plain
description: An extensive flat plain of glacial till that forms when a sheet of ice becomes detached from the main body of a glacier and melts in place depositing the sediments it carried.

label: flood plain
description: An area which is subject to periodic flooding.

label: floodway
description: The stream channel and adjacent areas that carry flood flows in a flood plain.

label: alluvial plain
description: A relatively flat and gently sloping landform found at the base of a range of hills or mountains, formed by the deposition of alluvial soil over a long period of time by one or more streams coming from the mountains.

label: lacustrine plain
description: A plain that originally formed in a lacustrine environment, that is, as the bed of a lake, but from which the water has disappeared, by natural drainage, evaporation or other geophysical processes.

label: fissure cave
description: A narrow, vertical cave passage, often developed along a joint but not necessarily so. Usually due to solution but sometimes to tension.

label: seamount
description: A mountain rising from the ocean seafloor that does not reach to the water's surface (sea level), and thus is not an island. Typically formed from volcanoes that rise abruptly and are usually found rising from a seafloor of 1,000 - 4,000 meters depth. Independent features that rise to at least 1,000 meters above the seafloor.

label: guyot
description: A flat-topped seamount.

label: submarine canyon
description: A steep-sided valley on the sea floor of the continental slope. Many submarine canyons are found as extensions to large rivers; however there are many that have no such association. Canyons cutting the continental slopes have been found at depths greater than 2 km below sea level. Many submarine canyons continue as submarine channels across continental rise areas and may extend for hundreds of kilometers.

label: continental slope
description: A slope which 1) is part of the seafloor and 2) extends from the end of the continental shelf (the shelf break) to the continental rise.

label: continental rise
description: On Earth, the gradient of the continental rise is on the order of 0.5-1. It may extend as far as 500 kilometers from the slope,

label: ocean trench
description: Hemispheric-scale long but narrow topographic depressions of the sea floor. They are the deepest parts of the ocean floor.

label: drumlin
description: An elongated whale-shaped hill formed by glacial action. Its long axis is parallel with the movement of the ice, with the blunter end facing into the glacial movement. Drumlins are sometimes compared to kames, but their formation is distinctively different. A drumlin is not originally shaped by meltwater, but by the ice itself and has a quite regular shape. It occurs in fine grained material, such as clay or shale, not in sands and gravels. And drumlins usually have concentric layers of material, as the ice successively plasters new layers in its movement.

label: dry lake
description: Classes like this pose a logical problem. This probably shouldn't be a lake (water body) but a depression. Lakes which have temporarily lost water should be distinguished from permanently dry lakes.
A lake that has either permanently or temporally lost its water.

label: dry stream
description: A stream channel through which no water flows and which has dried, containing no appreciable accumulations of water.

label: escarpment
description: An escarpment usually represents the line of erosional loss of the newer rock over the older.

label: fault escarpment
description: An escarpment resulting from a fault.

label: esker
description: A long, winding ridge of stratified sand and gravel which occur in glaciated and formerly glaciated regions of Europe and North America.

label: ridge
description: A long and narrow elevation with steep sides.

label: polder
description: An area reclaimed from the sea by diking and draining.

label: butte
description: An isolated hill with steep sides and a small flat top, smaller than mesas and plateaus. Buttes are formed by erosion when a cap of hard rock, usually of volcanic origin, covers a layer of softer rock that is easily worn away. This hard rock avoids erosion while the rock around it wears down.

label: horst
description: The raised fault block bounded by normal faults. The raised block is a portion of the Earth's crust that has remained stationary while the land has sunk on either side of it or has been crushed by a mountain range against it.

label: graben
description: A depressed block of land bordered by parallel faults. A graben is the result of a block of land being downthrown producing a valley with a distinct scarp on each side. Grabens often occur side-by-side with horsts. Horst and graben structures are indicative of tensional forces and crustal stretching.

label: drainage basin
description: An extent or area of land where surface water from rain and melting snow or ice converges to a single point at lower elevation, usually the exit of the basin, where the waters join another waterbody.

label: rift valley
description: A valley created by the formation of a rift, i.e. place where a planet's lithosphere is being pulled apart by tectonic forces.

label: shore
description: That part of the land in immediate contact with a body of water including the area between high and low water lines.

label: peninsula
description: A body of land jutting out into and nearly surrounded by water.

label: dune slack
description: A valley or trough between two dunes.

label: depressed landform
description: A landform sunken or depressed below the surrounding area.

label: meteor impact crater
description: For the moment, no distinction is made between meteroids, lithometeors, or meteorites in this class. These can be added if needed.
A crater caused by the impact of a meteor.

label: kettle
description: A fluvioglacial landform occurring as the result of blocks of ice calving from the front of a receding glacier and becoming partially to wholly buried by glacial outwash. Glacial outwash is generated when sediment laden streams of meltwater flow away from the glacier and are deposited to form broad outwash plains called sandurs. When the ice blocks melt, holes are left in the sandur.

label: sandur
description: The plain formed by the large amounts of silt and sediment, picked up as a glacier erodes the underlying rocks as it moves slowly downhill, and at the snout of the glacier, meltwater can carry this sediment away from the glacier and deposit it on a broad plain. The material in the outwash plain is often size-sorted by the water runoff of the melting glacier with the finest materials, like silt, being the most distantly re-deposited, whereas larger boulders are the closest to the original terminus of the glacier.

label: blowout
description: A sandy depression in a sand dune ecosystem (psammosere) caused by the removal of sediments by wind.

label: joint-plane cave
description: A cavity developed along a joint and elongate in cross-section.

label: volcanic cave
description: "Lave cave" is differentiated from "volcanic cave": the former is formed in volcanic rock, the latter is formed by volcanic processes.
A cave formed in volcanic rock.

label: live cave
description: A cave containing a stream or active speleothems.

label: outflow cave
description: A cave from which a stream flows or formerly did so and which cannot be followed upstream to the surface.

label: polje
description: A large closed depression draining underground, with a flat floor across which there may be an intermittent or perennial stream and which may be liable to flood and become a lake. The floor makes a sharp break with parts of surrounding slopes.

label: sea cave
description: A cave in present-day or emerged sea cliffs, formed by wave attack or solution.

label: speleothem
description: A secondary mineral deposit formed in caves, most commonly calcite.

label: stalagmite
description: A speleothem projecting vertically upwards from a cave floor and formed by precipitation from drips.

label: stalactite
description: A speleothem hanging downwards from a roof or wall, of cylindrical or conical form, usually with a central hollow tube.

label: doline
description: A closed depression draining underground in karst, of simple but variable form, e.g. cylindrical, conical, bowl- or dish-shaped. From a few to many hundreds of metres in dimensions.

label: subjacent karst
description: Karst developed in soluble beds underlying other rock formations; the surface may or may not be affected by the karst development.

label: syngenetic karst
description: Karst developed in eolian calcarenite when the development of karst features has taken place at the same time as the lithification of dune sand.

label: polygonal karst
description: Karst completely pitted by closed depressions so that divides between them form a crudely polygonal network.

label: doline karst
description: Karst dominated by closed depressions, chiefly dolines, perforating a simple surface.

label: ice cap dome
description: A comparatively elevated area on an icecap.

label: pyroclastic cone
description: A cone made of material ejected from a volcano. The material can range from finest particles. In comparison, cinder cones are more uniform. They are usually found in or on larger features, such as stratovolcanoes, shield volcanoes and can be found inside calderas, however they can also be an independent feature. They can range from a few metres in height and are usually formed by a single eruption.

label: massif
description: A section of the Earths's crust that is demarcated by faults or flexures. In the movement of the crust, a massif tends to retain its internal structure while being displaced as a whole.

label: lake shore
description: That part of the land in immediate contact with a lake.

label: container of an intermittent lake
description: This has been moved from the lake hierarchy.
A depression which intermittently contains a lake.

label: mountain spur
description: A spur which is part of a mountain.

label: land bridge
description: An isthmus or other land connection between what at other times are separate land masses which allows animals and plants to cross and colonise new lands. Land bridges are commonly created by regression, in which sea levels fall exposing previously submerged sections of continental shelf. Land bridges are also formed by: (a) upthrust at the edge of continental plates; and (b) glacial retreat alleviating pressure on shallow marine formations.

label: strait
description: A narrow channel of water that connects two larger bodies of water, and thus lies between two land masses.

label: channel of a watercourse
description: A depressed landform which physically confines a river, slough or ocean strait, and which consists of a bed and banks.

label: marine channel
description: A channel of a watercourse which contains marine water.

label: lake channel
description: A channel of a watercourse which contains lake water.

label: volcanic cone
description: Built by fragments (called ejecta) thrown up (ejected) from a volcanic vent, piling up around the vent in the shape of a cone with a central crater.

label: ash cone
description: A cone that is composed of particles of silt to sand size. Explosive eruptions from a vent where the magma is interacting with groundwater or the sea (as in an eruption off the coast) produce steam and are called phreatic. The interaction between the magma, expanding steam, and volcanic gases results in the ejection of mostly small particles called ash. Fallen ash has the consistency of flour. The unconsolidated ash forms an ash cone which becomes a tuff cone or tuff ring once the ash consolidates.

label: cinder cone
description: A cone built almost entirely of loose volcanic fragments called cinders (pumice, pyroclastics, or tephra). They are built from particles and blobs of congealed lava ejected from a single vent. As the gas-charged lava is blown violently into the air, it breaks into small fragments that solidify and fall as cinders around the vent to form a circular or oval cone. Most cinder cones have a bowl-shaped crater at the summit.

label: spatter cone
description: A volcanic cone formed of molten lava ejected from a vent somewhat like taffy. Expanding gases in the lava fountains tear the liquid rock into irregular gobs that fall back to earth, forming a heap around the vent. The still partly liquid rock splashed down and over the sides of the developing mound is called spatter. Because spatter is not fully solid when it lands, the individual deposits are very irregular in shape and weld together as they cool, and in this way particularly differ from cinder and ash.

label: kipuka
description: An elevated area such as a hill, ridge or old lava dome inside or downslope from an area of active volcanism. New lava flows will cover the surrounding land, isolating the kipuka so that it appears as a (usually) forested island in a barren lava flow.

label: pingo
description: Pingos may occur in cold-climate wetland areas, but are not necessarily wetlands themselves.
A mound of earth-covered ice found in the Arctic, subarctic, and Antarctica that can reach up to 70 metres in height and up to 2 kilometres in diameter.

label: natural arch
description: A natural formation where a rock arch forms, with a natural passageway through underneath.

label: raised beach
description: A beach or wave cut platform raised above the shore line by a relative fall in the sea level.

label: coastal dune
description: A dune which is part of a coast.

label: machair
description: A fertile low-lying raised beach found on the some of the coastlines of Ireland and Scotland, in particular in the Outer Hebrides.

label: ria
description: A submergent coastal landform that forms where sea levels rise relative to the land either as a result of eustatic sea level change; where the global sea levels rise or isostatic sea level change; where the land sinks. When this happens valleys which were previously at sea level become submerged.

label: stack
description: A geological landform consisting of a steep and often vertical column or columns of rock in the sea near a coast.

label: wave-cut platform
description: The narrow flat area often seen at the base of a sea cliff caused by the action of the waves.

label: limestone pavement
description: A natural karst landform consisting of a flat, incised surface of exposed limestone that resembles artificial pavement.

label: arete
description: A ridge which is jagged, narrow and separates glacier valleys or cirques.

The ridge frequently resembles the blade of a serrated knife. A French term referring to the bones in a fish backbone. Aretes are typically formed when two glaciers erode parallel U-shaped valleys. Aretes can also form when two glacial cirques erode towards one another, although frequently this results in a saddle-shaped pass, called a col.

label: dirt cone
description: A feature of a glacier, in which dirt, which has fallen into a hollow in the ice, forms a coating which insulates the ice below. The surrounding ice melts away, leaving the dirt cone.

label: monadnock
description: An isolated hill, knob, ridge, or small mountain that rises abruptly from a gently sloping or virtually level surrounding plain.

label: kame terrace
description: A terrace associated with a kame.

label: outwash fan
description: A fan-shaped body of sediments deposited by braided streams from a melting glacier.

label: tunnel valley
description: A deep but narrow valley with a 'U' shaped cross-section and frequently a 'U' shaped plan which is usually found filled with glacial till. It is formed when the edge of an ice mass advances up a slope. Its length may be appropriately measured in centimetres or kilometres, depending on the circumstances of formation.

label: Nye channel
description: A small tunnel valley.

label: alas
description: A steep-sided depression formed by the melting of permafrost; it may contain a lake.

label: dell
description: A small wooded valley, either U- or V-shaped.

label: rock shelter
description: A shallow cave-like opening at the base of a bluff or cliff.

label: terracette
description: A ridge on a hillside formed when saturated soil particles expand, then contract as they dry, causing them to move slowly downhill.

label: turlough
description: A container of an intermittent lake unique to the limestone areas of Ireland, mostly west of the River Shannon. Most turloughs flood in the autumn, usually some time in October, and then dry up some time between April and July.

label: penplain
description: A region of low topographic relief as a consequence of erosion by streams.

label: pseudocrater
description: A volcanic landform which resembles a true volcanic crater, but differs in that it is not an actual vent from which lava has erupted. A pseudocrater is characterised by the absence of any magma conduit which connects below the surface of the earth. Pseudocraters are formed by steam explosions as flowing hot lava crosses over a wet surface, such as a swamp, a lake, or a pond. The explosive gases break through the lava surface in a manner similar to a phreatic eruption, and the tephra builds up crater-like forms which can appear very similar to real volcanic craters.

label: harbour
description: Harbours are often used to store or shelter ships.

label: artificial harbor
description: A harbor constructed by human agency.

label: natural harbor
description: A harbor which is formed by a natural landform where a part of a body of water is protected and deep enough to furnish anchorage.

label: mount
description: This is not placed under surface landform, as seamounts are also mounts and are submerged.
A mountain or a hill.

label: peak
description: The summit of a mount.

label: pinnacle
description: A tall, slender, spire-shaped rock projecting from a level or more gently sloping surface.

label: sea shore
description: That part of the land in immediate contact with a sea, including the intertidal zone.

label: palsa
description: Palsas typically occur in areas with discontinuous permafrost, frequently peat bogs. A palsa consists, similarly to a pingo, of an ice core and overlying soil materials, in case of a palsa usually boggy soil. Palsas are characteristically found in areas with discontinuous permafrost and in such areas bay be the only reliable surface evidence of permafrost. A palsa needs large quantities of water for the formation of its ice core (i.e. ice lens), which is why they frequently emerge from and are bound by boggy soils, which can store enormous quantities of water in their pores. Palsas develop particularly in moorlands and are therefore also named palsamoors.
A frost heave which is formed as the result of a perennial ice lens forming under soil, pushing a roughly oval portion land surface upwards.

label: rill
description: A narrow and shallow incision into soil resulting from erosion by overland flow that has been focused into a thin thread by soil surface roughness. Rilling, the process of rill formation, is common on agricultural land and unvegetated ground.

label: trough
description: A linear structural depression that extends laterally over a distance, while being less steep than a trench. A trough can be a narrow basin or a geologic rift. There are various oceanic troughs, troughs found under oceans; examples include the rift along the mid-oceanic ridge and the Cayman Trough.

label: container of an intermittent saline lake
description: A depression that is periodically filled with saline water, forming a saline lake.

label: container of an intermittent oxbow lake
description: A depression which is continous with one or more abandoned meander loops of a river channel.

label: container of an intermittent pond
description: A container of an intermittent water body which, when filled with water, has a well-illuminated surface layer, is subject to complete mixing of the water it holds, and is smaller than the container of a lake.

label: intermittently filled reservoir
description: A reservoir that is not permanently filled with water, at times being dry.

label: terrace
description: A step-like feature between higher and lower ground: a relatively flat or gently inclined shelf of earth, backed and fronted by steep slopes or manmade detaining walls.

label: marine terrace
description: A terrace which is located in a marine water body.

label: meander neck
description: A landform which is the narrowest part of a meander.

label: crater
description: A generally circular saucer or bowl-shaped depression caused by explosive action.

label: hummock
description: A patch of ground, distinct from and slightly above the surrounding plain or wetland. Often occurs in groups.

label: agricultural terrace
description: A terrace which is used for agricultural activities.

label: landslide
description: A mound of earth material, at the base of a slope and the associated scoured area.

label: rockfall
description: An irregular mass of fallen rock at the base of a cliff or steep slope.

label: canal tunnel
description: A tunnel through which a canal passes.

label: cutoff
description: A channel formed as a result of a stream cutting through a meander neck.

label: abandoned watercourse
description: A former stream or distributary no longer carrying flowing water, but still evident due to lakes, wetland, topographic or vegetation patterns.

label: cliff cleft
description: A deep narrow slot, notch, or groove in a cliff.

label: interfluve
description: A relatively undissected upland between adjacent stream valleys.

label: ice cap ridge
description: A linear elevation on an icecap.

label: beach ridge
description: A ridge of sand just inland and parallel to the beach, usually in series.

label: apron
description: A gentle slope, with a generally smooth surface, particularly found around groups of islands and seamounts.

label: ice cap depression
description: A depression which is part of an ice cap.

label: landfill
description: A depression which contains objects and materials discarded by humans or their technologies.

label: riverine pothole
description: A depression which 1) has smooth surfaces, 2) has a bowl-like or cylindrical shape, 3) results from the erosion of the rocky bed of a watercourse.

label: moatan
description: An annular depression that may not be continuous, located at the base of many seamounts, islands, and other isolated elevations.

label: boulder field
description: A high altitude or high latitude bare, flat area covered with large angular rocks.

label: arrugado
description: An undersea area of subdued corrugations.

label: geographic sill
description: The low part of a gap or saddle separating basins.

label: kame
description: An irregularly shaped hill or mound composed of sorted or stratified sand and gravel that is deposited in contact with the glacial ice. It can have an irregular shape. Kames are often associated with kettles, and this is referred to as kame and kettle topography. When the ice retreats further, the delta kame often collapses. Kame terraces are frequently found along the side of a glacial valley and are the deposits of meltwater streams flowing between the ice and the adjacent valley side.

label: swale
description: The term can refer to a natural landscape feature or a human-created one. When created by humans, this open drain system is designed to manage water runoff.
A depression which comprises a low tract of land, especially when moist or marshy.

label: leat
description: A man-made watercourse, or makeshift aqueduct, often an artificial channel which supplies water to a watermill or its mill pond, collecting water from upstream of the mill so that the natural level of the driving water is above the level of the stream at the mill. Alternatively to may deliver water for mineral washing and concentration, irrigation or to a dye works.

label: shingle beach
description: A beach which is armoured with pebbles or small to medium sized cobbles.

label: container of an intermittent water body
description: This was formerly represented as a water body, which would not be valid during dry periods. This class more properly refers to the container of the water body, thusfar always some depression, which periodically contains a water body.
A depression which is is periodically filled with water when water supply exceeds evapotranspiration and bed seepage.

label: endorheic basin
description: A drainage basin from which there is no outflow of water, either on the surface as rivers, or underground by flow or diffusion through rock or permeable material.

label: talik
description: An area of unfrozen ground surrounded by permafrost.

label: calanque
description: A deep valley with steep sides, typically of limestone, in part submerged by the sea.

label: slope
description: A solid astronomical body part which is part of the planetary surface between the peak of an elevation or the bottom of a depression and relatively flat surrounding land.

label: alkaline hot spring
description: A alkaline spring through which groundwater, heated by geothermal energy, flows.

label: acidic hot spring
description: An acidic spring through which groundwater, heated by geothermal energy, flows.

label: mesophilic sulfur spring
description: A sulfur spring through which water at a temperature optimal for the growth of mesophillic microorganism (approximately 20 to 45 degrees Celsius) flows.

label: calcite hot spring
description: A calcic spring through which groundwater, heated by geothermal energy, flows.

label: neutral hot spring
description: A neutral spring through which groundwater, heated by geothermal energy, flows.

label: subsurface landform
description: A landform which is located under the surface of a landmass.

label: oil reservoir
description: A subsurface landform which contains fluid hydrocarbons in porous or fractured rock formations.

label: sandy beach
description: A beach which is primarily composed of sand.

label: unexploded-ordnance dump
description: A dump which contains ammunition, or other material intended for use during combat, that still has the potential to explode.

label: borehole
description: A channel which is constructed by removing materials from land or submerged beds.

label: back-arc basin
description: A depression in the sea floor that results from the collision of continental plates; the weight of the sinking plate causes the overlying plate to stretch and thin, causing a basin in the overlying plate. Sometimes, the Earth's crust in these basins stretches so much it cracks, allowing magma through from the mantle beneath. Hence, basins often contain active volcanoes and hydrothermal vents.

label: ocean basin
description:
This class is defined in its geological sense:
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ Hydrologically, an oceanic basin may be anywhere on Earth that is covered by seawater, but geologically ocean basins are large geologic basins that are below sea level. Geologically, there are other undersea geomorphological features such as the continental shelves, the deep ocean trenches, and the undersea mountain ranges (for example, the mid-Atlantic ridge) which are not considered to be part of the ocean basins; while hydrologically, oceanic basins include the flanking continental shelves and shallow, epeiric seas.
A structural basin that is below sea level.

label: karst field
description: A large flat plain in karst territory with areas usually 5 to 400 sqaure kilometres.

label: ice rise
description: An ice rise is an elevation which is part of an ice shelf, typically dome shared, and formed by the ice shelf overriding an obstruction in the seabed. An ice rise may be adjacent only to an ice shelf, or to an ice shelf and a sea. For some features, properly ice rises, the term island has become established through usage.

label: karst cave
description: A cave which is part of a karst formation.

label: dry stream valley
description: A dry valley which was formed as a result of erosion due to stream formation and flow.

label: dry river valley
description: A dry stream valley which was formed as a result of erosion due to river formation and flow.

label: marine hydrothermal vent
description: A marine hydrothermal vent is a marine benthic feature where heat generated due to tectonic activity, either at divergent plate boundaries or convergent ocean plates where back-arc spreading occurs, is released or 'vented' to the surface. The resultant high temperature water jets are laden with dissolved metals and minerals.

label: marine hydrothermal vent chimney
description: A column of solid material which has been progressively deposited around a hydrothermal vent.

label: marine pockmark
description: Pockmarks are craters in the seabed resulting from the release of gas or liquid. Generally, they are formed in soft, fine-grained seabed sediments by the escape of fluids (gas or water, but mainly methane) into the water column.

label: mineral deposit
description: Note that the definition of the term mineral is debatable; however, a mineral generally must be naturally occuring, stable at room temperature, representable by a chemical formula (unlike rocks, which may include a wide variety of components), are usually formed by geophysical processes (i.e. are abiogenic), and have an ordered atomic arrangement.
A mineral deposit is a physiographic feature which has unusually high concentrations of one or more minerals.

label: white smoker
description: A hydrothermal vent found on the ocean floor which emits lighter-hued minerals, such as those containing barium, calcium and silicon. These alkaline hydrothermal vents also continuously generate acetyl thioesters, providing both the starting point for more complex organic molecules and the energy needed to produce them.

label: seep
description: A seep is a spring in which water has filtered through permeable earth to the surface.

label: cold seep
description:
MERGED DEFINITION:
TARGET DEFINITION: A cold seep is a seep in which methane and other hydrocarbon-rich fluids rise to the sea floor.
--------------------
SOURCE DEFINITION: An area of the ocean floor where hydrogen sulfide, methane and other hydrocarbon-rich fluid seepage occurs. Cold seeps are distinct from hydrothermal vents: the former's emissions are of the same temperature as the surrounding seawater, whereas the latter's emissions are super-heated.

label: hydrothermal seep
description: A hydrothermal seep is a seep in which diffuse flow of geothermally heated fluids with high methane concentrations. This seep has been proposed as an intermediate between cold seeps and hydrothermal vents.

label: structural basin
description: A structural basin is a geological depression formed by tectonic warping of previously flat lying rock strata.

label: pingo scar
description: A depression caused by the collapse of a pingo.

label: continental margin
description: On Earth, continental margins constitute about 28% of the oceanic area.

label: outcrop
description: A portion of environmental material which protrudes through a surface layer.

This is kept as a general class. One can specify subclasses by identifying the protruding material (e.g. rock outcroup, mineral outcrop, etc ) and the material(s) the protrusion emerges from. Possible logical definition:   A portion of ENVO:environmental material which has_quality PATO:"protruding out of" a ENVO:surface layer of an ENVO:environmental material.

label: rocky slope
description: A rocky slope is a slope which has a surface primarily composed of rock.

label: gravelly slope
description: A gravelly slope is a slope which has a surface primarily composed of gravel.

label: hillside
description: A hillside is a slope that is part of a hill.

label: talus slope
description: A talus slope is a slope which has a surface layer composed of scree.

label: limestone cave
description: A cave formed in limestone, usually by dissolution of limestone by acidic groundwater.
Can be linked to a solutional environmental process and acidic groundwater.

label: solutional cave
description: Can be linked to a solutional environmental process and acidic groundwater.
A cave formed by the dissolution of soluble rock or other solid material such as limestone, chalk, dolomite, gypsum, salt or marble.

label: primary cave
description: A cave formed at the same time as the surrounding rock.

label: inflationary cave
description: A cave that is formed by the action of pressurised lava pushing against surrounding rock and then draining away.

label: erosional cave
description: A cave formed by erosion caused by flowing streams carrying rocks or sediments.

label: glacier cave
description: A glacier cave is a cave formed within or under a glacier.

label: ice cave
description: An ice cave is a bedrock cave which contains year-round ice formations.

label: talus cave
description: A talus cave is a cave formed by the openings between large boulders which have fallen into a random heap.

label: anchialine cave
description: An anchialine cave is a cave which contains an anchialine pool.

label: vadose cave
description: A cave which is within a vadose zone.

label: burrow
description: Should be better defined logically aggregating 'hole' or 'tunnel' with some sort of relation to 'habitation' etc.
A burrow is a hole or tunnel excavated into the ground by an animal to create a space suitable for habitation, temporary refuge, or as a byproduct of locomotion

label: ravine
description: A ravine is a small, narrow, steep-sided valley that is larger than a gully and smaller than a canyon and that is usually worn by running water.

label: salt glacier
description: A mass of salt which has erupted onto a planetary surface, usually through sedimentary rock.

label: salt dome
description: A dome-shaped mass of salt formed when a thick bed of evaporite minerals (mainly salt, or halite) found at depth intrudes vertically into surrounding rock strata, forming a diapir.

label: latrine pit
description: A latrine pit is typically at least 3 metres (10 feet) deep and 1 metre (3.2 feet) across.
A latrine pit is an artificial hole or cavity in the ground used to collect human excreta.

label: freshwater spring
description: A spring through which fresh water flows.

label: trench
description: A trench is a type of excavation or depression in the ground that is generally deeper than it is wide (as opposed to a wider gully or ditch), and narrow compared to its length (as opposed to a simple hole).

label: stream channel
description: A channel of a watercourse which contains a stream.

label: ocean strait
description: An ocean strait is a strait which connects two oceans.

label: river channel
description: A stream channel which contains a river.

label: undersea trough
description: An undersea trough is a trough which is below a marine water body.

label: tuff cone
description: A cone that is composed of consolidated volcanic ash.

label: igneous extrusion
description: A mass of igneous rock formed when hot magma flows out (extrudes) onto a planetary surface as lava or explodes violently into the atmosphere to fall back as pyroclastics or tuff.

label: fumarole-derived ice tower
description: A hollow tower of ice formed by the freezing of steam escaping a fumarole.

label: plumbing drain
description: An artificial channel which transports unwanted water or waste liquids away from their source, either to a more useful area, a receptacle, or into sewers or stormwater mains as waste discharge to be released or processed.

label: vegetated hill
description: A hill which has a surface that is partially or wholly covered by plant communities.
This class will be axiomatised to coordinate with the 'vegetated area' class.

label: channel of an intermittent river
description: A channel of an intermittent stream which contains a river when water supply exceeds evapotranspiration and bed seepage.

label: channel of an intermittent stream
description: A channel through which a directional flow of water periodically occurs, ceasing when bed seepage or evapotranspiration exceed the available water supply.

label: dry river
description: See http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO_01000979 for the channel of an intermittent river.
A dry stream channel through which a river had flowed, but now contains no appreciable accumulations of water.

label: impact crater
description: A crater which was formed as a result of the impact of one astronomical body on another.

label: fossil worm burrow
description: A channel which was formed as a result of an annelid burrowing through soil, where organic residues lining the burrow have subsequently initiated fossilization.

label: desert
description: A landform which has been rendered barren or partially barren by environmental extremes, especially by low rainfall, and which loses more liquid water by evapotranspiration than is supplied by precipitation.

label: terrestrial mountain
description: A mountain which is located on land and which is bounded by an atmosphere or outer space.

label: polar mountain
description: A mountain that is part of a polar environment.

label: temperate mountain
description: A mountain that is part of a temperate environment.

label: tropical mountain
description: A mountain that is part of a tropical environment.

label: high-elevation mountain
description: On Earth, mountains in this category cross the atmospheric oxycline above which oxygen concentrations fall below the physiological tolerance threshold of most humans. Note that the threshold elevations are inconsistent between the various reports which list this classification: while some have overlapping thresholds, others are non-overlapping. The latter model is used in ENVO for coherence and to adhere to the Kapos et al. 2000 reference.
A mountain which has a maximum elevation greater than 2500 metres above sea level.

label: mid-elevation mountain
description: On Earth, mountains in this category are below the atmospheric oxycline above which oxygen concentrations fall below the physiological tolerance threshold of most humans. Note that the threshold elevations are inconsistent between the various reports which list this classification: while some have overlapping thresholds, others are non-overlapping. The latter model is used in ENVO for coherence and to adhere to the Kapos et al. 2000 reference.
A mountain which has a maximum elevation between 300 and 2499 metres above sea level and slopes greater than or equal to two degrees of inclination.

label: UNEP-WCMC class 1 mountain
description: A high-elevation mountain which has a maximum elevation greater than 4500 metres above sea level.

label: UNEP-WCMC class 2 mountain
description: A high-elevation mountain which has a maximum elevation between 3500 and 4500 metres above sea level.

label: UNEP-WCMC class 3 mountain
description: A high-elevation mountain which has a maximum elevation between 2500 and 3500 metres above sea level.

label: UNEP-WCMC class 4 mountain
description: A mid-elevation mountain which has a maximum elevation between 1500 and 2499 metres above sea level and a slope greater than or equal to two degrees.

label: UNEP-WCMC class 5 mountain
description: A mid-elevation mountain which has a maximum elevation between 1000 and 1499 metres above sea level and either 1) a slope greater than or equal to five degrees or 2) a local elevation range, within a 7 kilometre radius, of greater than 300 metres above sea level.

label: UNEP-WCMC class 6 mountain
description: A mid-elevation mountain which has a maximum elevation between 300 and 999 metres above sea level and a local elevation range, within a 7 kilometre radius, of greater than 300 metres above sea level.

label: UNEP-WCMC class 7 mountain
description: This is an odd class, as it's not a mountain in itself but is used to classify elevated basins and plateaus surrounded by mountains.
An elevated inner basin or plateau surrounded by mountains, but not - itself - a mountain.

label: spur
description: A slope of land descending laterally from a hill, mountain or main crest of a ridge.

label: flattened elevation
description: An elevation which is flattened across its highest surface.

label: sea ice hummock
description: An elevation which is formed by pressure at the point of contact between ice floes, resulting in a conglomeration of broken ice.

Sea ice hummocks may be fresh or weathered. The weathering of hummocks is similar to young mountain peaks with steep slopes that erode into smooth, rolling hills, in this case during the summer melt season.  The submerged volume of broken ice under the hummock, forced downwards by pressure, is termed a bummock.

label: frost-formed hummock
description: A hummock which is primarily composed of soil that has been pushed up by frost action.

Permafrost hummocks are often found in uniformly spaced large groups. Hummocks can form in areas of permafrost or seasonally frozen ground, and are one of the most common surface features of the Arctic.

label: frost heave
description: An elevation which is formed as an ice mass forms under soil, resulting in upwards deformation of the land surface.

label: pit
description: A depression in the ground resembling a hole or cavity, either natural or anthropogenic.

label: manure pit
description: A pit which is used for the collection and storage of manure.

label: surface landform
description: A landform which occurs on the surface of an astronomical body.

label: submerged landform
description: A landform which is submerged underneath a body of liquid.

label: calcic spring
description: A mineral spring through which water with elevated concentrations of calcium hydroxide flows.

label: lithia spring
description: A mineral spring through which water with elevated concentrations of lithium salts flows.

label: chalybeate spring
description: A spring through which water with elevated concentrations of iron salts flows.

label: alum spring
description: A spring through which water with elevated concentrations of hydrated double sulfate aluminium salts flows.

label: salt spring
description: A mineral spring through which water with elevated concentrations of sodium, calcium, or magnesium salts flows.

label: alkaline spring
description: A mineral spring through which water with a high pH flows.

label: soda spring
description: A mineral spring through which water with elevated levels of dissolved carbon dioxide gas flows.

label: radioactive spring
description: A mineral spring through which water with elevated levels of radioactive material flows.

label: neutral spring
description: A spring through which water with a neutral pH flows.

label: acidic spring
description: A spring through which water with a low pH flows.

label: uranium deposit
description: A mineral deposit that contains uranium ore.

label: natural nuclear fission reactor
description: Oklo is the only known location for this in the world and consists of 16 sites at which self-sustaining nuclear fission reactions are thought to have taken place approximately 1.7 billion years ago, and ran for a few hundred thousand years, averaging probably less than 100 kW of thermal power during that time
A uranium deposit where self-sustaining nuclear chain reactions have occurred.

label: geographic basin
description: A depression which is part of a planetary crust, is of geographic scale, and is partially or completely enclosed.

label: cryoconite hole
description: This class doesn't refer to the site but instead the depression or hole and therefore the adjacency to the cryoconite itself.
A vertical thaw hole within an ice mass, formed as a result of ice melt associated with local temperature increases, due to increased absorption of solar radiation by cryoconite deposits.

label: brine channel
description: A channel through which brine flows.

label: thaw hole
description: A channel which traverses an ice mass floating on a water body and bridges the atmosphere to the underlying water through its internal cavity.

label: thermokarst depression
description: A geographic basin which is formed due to the erosion of thermokarst by meltwater released from thawing permafrost.

label: permafrost crater derived from a methane explosion
description: A crater which is found in permafrost and formed as a result of an explosion fuelled by methane formerly contained in that permafrost.

label: channel
description: A structure which traverses a mass of one or more environmental materials, and encloses a roughly tubular site.

label: hillock
description: Hillocks are similar in their distribution and size to small mesas or buttes.
A hill which is small and usually separated from a larger group of hills such as a range.

label: riverfront
description: A shore along a river.

label: fermentation pit
description: A pit which has been constructed for use in fermentation processes that will yield alcoholic spirits.

label: alcohol fermentation pit
description: A fermentation pit which is constructed to facilitate the fermentation of alcoholic substances.
Definition from 2021-08-05 call with Buttigieg, Duncan and Miller

label: clay fermentation pit
description: A fermentation pit which is constructed from clay.
Definition from 2021-08-05 call with Buttigieg, Duncan and Miller

label: subtropical grassland biome
description: A subtropical grassland in which dominant ecological communities have reached their climax successional state.

label: tropical grassland biome
description: Preliminary definition. The semantics and definitions of "mediterranean", "subtropical", "tropical", "temperate", "polar", and similar climate types may be transferred to an "environmental condition" class once the semantics of this class have been established.

label: temperate grassland biome
description: Preliminary definition. The semantics and definitions of "mediterranean", "subtropical", "tropical", "temperate", "polar", and similar climate types may be transferred to an "environmental condition" class once the semantics of this class have been established.

label: montane grassland biome
description: A montane grassland biome is a grassland biome which occurs in regions elevated above sea level and which has community structure determined by elevation-dependent environmental conditions.
Preliminary definition.

label: mediterranean grassland biome
description: A subtropical grassland biome which includes communities adapted to hot to warm, dry summers, mild to cold, rainy winters, and the influence of large, usually marine, bodies of water.

Preliminary definition. The semantics and definitions of "mediterranean", "subtropical", "tropical", "temperate", "polar", and similar climate types may be transferred to an "environmental condition" class once the semantics of this class have been established.

label: mine tailing
description: Mine tailings are the materials left over after the process of separating the valuable fraction from the uneconomic fraction (gangue) of an ore.

label: permafrost
description: An environmental material which is 1) composed primarily of soil or rock and included ice or organic material and 2) at or below the freezing point of water for two or more years.

label: scree
description: Broken rock that appears at the bottom of crags, mountain cliffs or valley shoulders.

label: vomit material
description: ENVO bodily fluid classes differ from UBERON's treatment of bodily fluids. UBERON refers to the substance itself ("S"). We assert that UBERON's classes are the primary compositional component of the terms in ENVO ("S material"). Use of the ENVO terms is typically recommended when you wish to indicate that there may be other materials intermixed with S.
A bodily fluid material which is composed primarily of vomit, a bodily fluid consisting of the expulsed contents of the stomach of an organism disgorged through the mouth or nose.

label: lake sediment
description: Lake sediment is sediment which covers the bottom of a lake. Lake sediments are comprised mainly of clastic material (sediment of clay, silt, and sand sizes), organic debris, chemical precipitates, or combinations of these.

label: rock
description: From https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ [A mineral] is different from a rock, which can be an aggregate of minerals or non-minerals and does not have a specific chemical composition. The exact definition of a mineral is under debate, especially with respect to the requirement a valid species be abiogenic, and to a lesser extent with regards to it having an ordered atomic structure.
A rock is a naturally occurring solid aggregate of one or more minerals or mineraloids.

label: soil
description: An environmental material which is primarily composed of minerals, varying proportions of sand, silt, and clay, organic material such as humus, interstitial gases, liquids, and a broad range of resident micro- and macroorganisms.

label: waste water
description: Water that has been adversely affected in quality by anthropogenic influence.

label: fecal material
description: ENVO bodily fluid classes differ from UBERON's treatment of bodily fluids. UBERON refers to the substance itself ("S"). We assert that UBERON's classes are the primary compositional component of the terms in ENVO ("S material"). Use of the ENVO terms is typically recommended when you wish to indicate that there may be other materials intermixed with S.
This is distinct from classes such as http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/UBERON_0001988 in that it refers to the environmental material composed primarily of feces rather than 'just' feces.
An excreta material which is composed primarily of feces, an excreta consisting of waste products expelled from an animal's digestive tract through the anus (or cloaca) during defecation.

label: air
description: The mixture of gases (roughly (by molar content/volume: 78% nitrogen, 20.95% oxygen, 0.93% argon, 0.038% carbon dioxide, trace amounts of other gases, and a variable amount (average around 1%) of water vapor) that surrounds the planet Earth.

label: liquid water
description: An environmental material primarily composed of dihydrogen oxide in its liquid form.

label: sediment
description: Sediment is typically deposited on the bed or bottom of a body of water or other liquid.
Particulate environmental material which is formed as a result of the transport and deposition of particles by flowing liquid.

label: dust
description: Dust occurs in and may be deposited from the atmosphere.
Particulate environmental material with diameters less than 500 micrometers.

label: saline water
description: The threshold salt concentration for classifying water as saline varies, but typically begins at about 1,000 to 3,000 parts salt per million parts water or 0.1–0.3% salt by weight.
Water which contains a significant concentration of dissolved salts.

label: fresh water
description: The lower bound of solute concentration required for water to be considered freshwater is variable, but is always less than that of seawater, and often cited as less than 1 gram of solutes per 1 litre of water.
Water which has a low concentration of dissolved solutes, particularly that of sodium chloride.

label: hypersaline water
description: The average salinity of sea water is assumed to be around 35,000 ppm, equivalent to 35 grams of salt per one liter (or kilogram) of water.
Water which contains a highly increased concentration of dissolved salts, surpassing the average salinity of seawater.

label: igneous rock
description: Rock formed from molten magma.

label: plutonic rock
description: An igneous rock that results from the crystallization of a magma below the surface of the Earth.

label: volcanic rock
description: Due to the general suggestion that volcanic rock simply comes from a volcanic process, it's not immediately clear whether this is interchangeable with igneous rock.
An igneous rock that results from magma reaching the surface either as lava or fragmental ejecta.

label: sedimentary rock
description: A rock formed by deposition of either clastic sediments, organic matter, or chemical precipitates (evaporites), followed by compaction of the particulate matter and cementation during diagenesis.

label: metamorphic rock
description: A rock formed by subjecting any rock type (including previously-formed metamorphic rock) to different temperature and pressure conditions than those in which the original rock was formed. These temperatures and pressures are always higher than those at the Earth's surface and must be sufficiently high so as to change the original minerals into other mineral types or else into other forms of the same minerals (e.g. by recrystallisation).

label: sewage
description: Wastewater that is contaminated with feces or urine,

label: brackish water
description: Water which has a higher salinity than fresh water but a lower salinity than marine water.

label: surface water
description: Water that is found on the surface of an astronomical object.

label: sludge
description: The residual semi-solid material left from domestic or industrial processes, or wastewater treatment processes.

label: anaerobic sediment
description: Sediment characterised by the absence of oxygen.

label: urine material
description: ENVO bodily fluid classes differ from UBERON's treatment of bodily fluids. UBERON refers to the substance itself ("S"). We assert that UBERON's classes are the primary compositional component of the terms in ENVO ("S material"). Use of the ENVO terms is typically recommended when you wish to indicate that there may be other materials intermixed with S.
An excreta material which is composed primarily of urine, a liquid excreta containing water and waste products made by the kidneys, stored in the bladder, and leaves the body through the urethra.

label: limestone
description: A sedimentary rock which is composed primarily of calcium carbonate in the form of calcite or aragnoite.

label: chalk
description: Limestone which is soft, white, and porous.

label: sandstone
description: A sedimentary rock composed mainly of sand-size mineral or rock grains.

label: shale
description: A fine-grained sedimentary rock whose original constituents were clays or muds. It is characterized by thin laminae breaking with an irregular curving fracture, often splintery and usually parallel to the often-indistinguishable bedding plane.

label: biosolids
description: A treated form of sludge, sometimes used as a fertilizer in agriculture.

label: oil sludge
description: A solid or gel in motor oil caused by the oil gelling or solidifying, usually at temperatures lower than 100deg C.

label: deep marine sediment
description: Sediment that accumulates in the flat or very gently sloping areas of the deep ocean basin floor. The three main types of deep marine sediment, also known as pelagic sediment, are siliceous oozes, calcareous oozes, and red clays.

label: chemically enriched sediment
description: Sediment which has increased levels of one or more chemical compounds.

label: petroleum enriched sediment
description: Organically enriched sediment which has increased levels of petroleum.

label: contaminated soil
description: A portion of contaminated soil is a portion of soil with elevated levels of some contaminant.
"contaminant" is more of a disposition - any material entity can be a contaminant in particular circumstances.

label: creosote contaminated soil
description: Soil which has elevated concentrations of creosote.

label: arsenic-rich mud
description: Mud which has elevated concentrations of arsenic.

label: stream sediment
description: Revise adjacent to. Consider sampled stream sediment. Dry stream sediment.

label: anaerobic mud
description: Mud which has no or neglible concentrations of dissolved oxygen.

label: leachate
description: The liquid produced when water percolates through any permeable material. It can contain either dissolved or suspended material, or usually both.

label: chromate contaminated soil
description: Soil which has elevated concentrations of chromate.

label: xylene contaminated soil
description: Soil which has elevated concentrations of xylene.

label: coal mine lake sediment
description: Coal mine lake sediment is lake sediment which covers the bottom of a coal mine lake.

label: sea water
description: This definition refers to water that is actually in a sea or ocean. This water may have a wide range of salinity levels.
Water which has physicochemical properties that have been determined by the processes occuring in a sea or ocean.

label: coastal sea water
description: Coastal sea water is sea water that is adjacent to a coast.

The limits of what qualifies as "adjacent to" vary greatly. This should be defined on a data level and is left intentionally fuzzy here. The label is "coastal sea water" rather than "coastal water" as some large lakes are often said to have coasts.

label: estuarine mud
description: Mud which is part of an estuary.

label: fossil material
description: A solid environmental material which is formed by the replacement of organic substances (including those in soils and sediments) with mineral material.

label: compost
description: Manure which has been derived from the aerobically decomposed remnants of organic materials.

label: naphthalene enriched sediment
description: Organically enriched sediment which has increased levels of naphthalene.

label: nitrobenzene enriched sediment
description: Organically enriched sediment which has increased levels of nitrobenzene.

label: animal litter
description: Straw or other material strewn in an animal's enclosure (e.g. a stable) for it to sleep on and to absorb its faeces and urine.

label: sea ice
description: Water ice which has formed by the freezing of sea water.

In the United States, NOAA sea ice operations does not include superstructure icing as being sea ice. In sea ice operations however, sea ice is any form of ice found at sea which has originated from the freezing of sea water. It presents the main kind of floating ice encountered at sea. Except where it forms ridges, sea ice is up to a few metres thick, in which respect it differs from shelf ice.  Sea ice may be discontinuous pieces (ice floes) moved on the ocean surface by wind and currents (pack ice), or a motionless sheet attached to the coast (land-fast ice). In brief, it forms first as lolly ice (frazil crystals), thickens into sludge, and coagulates into sheet ice, pancake ice, or into floes of various shapes and sizes. Thereafter, sea ice may develop into pack ice and/or become a form of pressure ice.  Sea ice less than one year old is called first-year ice. Perennial ice is sea ice that survives at least one summer. It may be subdivided into second-year ice and multi-year ice, where multiyear ice has survived at least two summers.

label: cis-dichloroethane contaminated sediment
description: Organically enriched sediment which has increased levels of cis-dichloroethane.

label: organically enriched sediment
description: Chemically-enriched sediment which has increased levels of organic compounds.

label: inorganically enriched sediment
description: Chemically-enriched sediment which has increased levels of inorganic compounds.

label: saline lake sediment
description: Saline lake sediment is sediment which covers the bottom of a saline lake.

label: oligotrophic water
description: Water which has very low concentrations of nutrients.

label: eutrophic water
description: Water with a high nutrient level.

label: mesotrophic water
description: Water with a nutrient level intermediate between eutrophic and oligotrophic.

label: arenosol
description: Arenosols are sandy soils, including both soils developed in residual sands after in situ weathering of usually quartz-rich sediments or rock, and soils developed in recently deposited sands such as dunes in deserts and beach lands.

label: anthrosol
description: Anthrosols comprise soils that have been modified profoundly through human activities, such as addition of organic materials or household wastes, irrigation and cultivation.

label: alisol
description: Alisols are soils that have a higher clay content in the subsoil than in the topsoil as a result of pedogenetic processes (especially clay migration) leading to an argic subsoil horizon. Alisols have a low base saturation at certain depths and high-activity clays throughout the argic horizon. They lack the albeluvic tonguing as in Albeluvisols. They occur predominantly in humid tropical, humid subtropical and warm temperate regions.

label: andosol
description: Andosols are soils that develop in volcanic ejecta or glasses under almost any climate (except under hyperarid climate conditions). However, Andosols may also develop in other silicate-rich materials under acid weathering in humid and perhumid climates.

label: albeluvisol
description: Albeluvisols are soils that have, beginning within 1 m of the soil surface, a clay illuviation horizon with an irregular or broken upper boundary resulting in tonguing of bleached soil material into the illuviation horizon.

label: acrisol
description: Acrisols are soils that have a higher clay content in the subsoil than in the topsoil as a result of pedogenetic processes (especially clay migration) leading to an argic subsoil horizon. Acrisols have in certain depths a low base saturation and low-activity clays.

label: cambisol
description: Cambisols combine soils with at least an incipient subsurface soil formation. Transformation of parent material is evident from structure formation and mostly brownish discoloration, increasing clay percentage, and/or carbonate removal.

label: cryosol
description: Cryosols comprise mineral soils formed in a permafrost environment. Where water is present, it occurs primarily in the form of ice. Cryogenic processes are the dominant soil-forming processes.

label: chernozem
description: Chernozems are soils with a thick black surface layer that is rich in organic matter.

label: durisol
description: Durisols are associated mainly with old surfaces in arid and semi-arid environments and accommodate very shallow to moderately deep, moderately well- to well-drained soils that contain cemented secondary silica (SiO2) within 100 cm of the soil surface.

label: calcisol
description: Calcisols are soils in which there is substantial secondary accumulation of lime. Calcisols are common in highly calcareous parent materials and widespread in arid and semi-arid environments.

label: kastanozem
description: Kastanozems are dry grassland soils, among them the zonal soils of the short-grass steppe belt, south of the Eurasian tall-grass steppe belt with Chernozems. Kastanozems have a similar profile to that of Chernozems but the humus-rich surface horizon is thinner and not as dark as that of the Chernozems and they show more prominent accumulation of secondary carbonates.

label: leptosol
description: Leptosols are very shallow soils over continuous rock and soils that are extremely gravelly and/or stony. Leptosols are azonal soils and particularly common in mountainous regions.

label: lixisol
description: Lixisols are soils that have a higher clay content in the subsoil than in the topsoil as a result of pedogenetic processes (especially clay migration) leading to an argic subsoil horizon. Lixisols have a high base saturation and low-activity clays at certain depths.

label: histosol
description: Histosols comprise soils formed in organic material. These vary from soils developed in predominantly moss peat in boreal, arctic and subarctic regions, via moss peat, reeds/ sedge peat (fen) and forest peat in temperate regions to mangrove peat and swamp forest peat in the humid tropics. Histosols are found at all altitudes, but the vast majority occurs in lowlands.

label: gleysol
description: Gleysols are wetland soils that, unless drained, are saturated with groundwater for long enough periods to develop a characteristic gleyic colour pattern. This pattern is essentially made up of reddish, brownish or yellowish colours at ped surfaces and/or in the upper soil layer or layers, in combination with greyish/bluish colours inside the peds and/or deeper in the soil.

label: gypsisol
description: Gypsisols are soils with substantial secondary accumulation of gypsum (calcium sulfate). These soils are found in the driest parts of the arid climate zone.

label: ferralsol
description: Ferralsols represent the classical, deeply weathered, red or yellow soils of the humid tropics. These soils have diffuse horizon boundaries, a clay assemblage dominated by low-activity clays (mainly kaolinite) and a high content of sesquioxides.

label: nitisol
description: Nitisols are deep, well-drained, red, tropical soils with diffuse horizon boundaries and a subsurface horizon with more than 30 percent clay and moderate to strong angular blocky structure elements that easily fall apart into characteristic shiny, polyhedric (nutty) elements. Weathering is relatively advanced but Nitisols are far more productive than most other red, tropical soils.

label: luvisol
description: Luvisols are soils that have a higher clay content in the subsoil than in the topsoil as a result of pedogenetic processes (especially clay migration) leading to an argic subsoil horizon. Luvisols have high-activity clays throughout the argic horizon and a high base saturation at certain depths.

label: phaeozem
description: Phaeozems accommodate soils of relatively wet grassland and forest regions in moderately continental climates. Phaeozems are much like Chernozems and Kastanozems but are leached more intensively. Consequently, they have dark, humus rich surface horizons that, in comparison with Chernozems and Kastanozems, are less rich in bases. Phaeozems may or may not have secondary carbonates but have a high base saturation in the upper metre of the soil.

label: plinthosol
description: Plinthosols are soils with plinthite, petroplinthite or pisoliths. Plinthite is an Fe-rich (in some cases also Mn-rich), humus-poor mixture of kaolinitic clay (and other products of strong weathering such as gibbsite) with quartz and other constituents that changes irreversibly to a layer with hard nodules, a hardpan or irregular aggregates on exposure to repeated wetting and drying. Petroplinthite is a continuous, fractured or broken sheet of connected, strongly cemented to indurated nodules or mottles. Pisoliths are discrete strongly cemented to indurated nodules. Both petroplinthite and pisoliths develop from plinthite by hardening.

label: planosol
description: Planosols are soils with a light-coloured, surface horizon that shows signs of periodic water stagnation and abruptly overlies a dense, slowly permeable subsoil with significantly more clay than the surface horizon.

label: solonchak
description: Solonchaks are soils that have a high concentration of soluble salts at some time in the year. Solonchaks are largely confined to the arid and semi-arid climate zones and to coastal regions in all climates.

label: umbrisol
description: Umbrisols are soils in which organic matter has accumulated within the mineral surface soil (in most cases with low base saturation) to the extent that it significantly affects the behaviour and utilization of the soil.

label: vertisol
description: A soil in which there is a high content of expansive clay known as montmorillonite that forms deep cracks in drier seasons or years. Alternate shrinking and swelling causes self-mulching, where the soil material consistently mixes itself, causing vertisols to have an extremely deep A horizon and no B horizon.

label: solonetz
description: Solonetz are soils with a dense, strongly structured, clayey subsurface horizon that has a high proportion of adsorbed Na and/or Mg ions. Solonetz that contain free soda (Na2CO3) are strongly alkaline (field pH > 8.5).

label: regosol
description: Regosols form a taxonomic remnant group containing all soils that could not be accommodated in any of the other RSGs. In practice, Regosols are very weakly developed mineral soils in unconsolidated materials that do not have a mollic or umbric horizon, are not very shallow or very rich in gravels (Leptosols), sandy (Arenosols) or with fluvic materials (Fluvisols). Regosols are extensive in eroding lands, particularly in arid and semi-arid areas and in mountainous terrain.

label: podzol
