description: Podzols are soils with a typically ash-grey upper subsurface horizon, bleached by loss of organic matter and iron oxides, on top of a dark accumulation horizon with brown, reddish or black illuviated humus and/or reddish Fe compounds. Podzols occur in humid areas in the boreal and temperate zones and locally also in the tropics.

label: loam
description: A soil which is composed of approximately equal proportions of sand and silt, with a smaller proportion of clay.
Some authorities consider loam to be any soil material that contains 7 to 27% clay, 28 to 50% silt, and less than 52% sand.

label: agricultural soil
description: Soil which is part of an ecosystem used for agricultural activities.

label: dune soil
description: Soil which is part of some dune.

label: forest soil
description: A portion of soil which is found in a forested area.

label: clay soil
description: Soil which is primarily composed of clay.

label: garden soil
description: A portion of soil which is found in a garden.

label: waste material
description: A material which is not the desired output of a process and which is typically the input of a process which removes it from its producer (e.g. a disposal process).

label: industrial waste material
description: Industrial wastes are liquid, solid and gaseous wastes originating from the manufacture of specific products.

label: fluvisol
description: Fluvisols accommodate genetically young, azonal soils in alluvial deposits.

label: stagnosol
description: Stagnosols are soils with a perched water table showing redoximorphic features caused by surface water. Stagnosols are periodically wet and mottled in the topsoil and subsoil, with or without concretions and/or bleaching.

label: technosol
description: Technosols are soils whose properties and pedogenesis are dominated by their technical origin. They contain a significant amount of artefacts (something in the soil recognizably made or extracted from the earth by humans), or are sealed by technic hard rock (material created by humans, having properties unlike natural rock). They include soils from wastes (landfills, sludge, cinders, mine spoils and ashes), pavements with their underlying unconsolidated materials, soils with geomembranes and constructed soils in human-made materials.

label: hay
description: Hay is grass, legumes or other herbaceous plants that have been cut, dried, and stored for use as animal fodder, particularly for grazing livestock such as cattle, horses, goats, and sheep.

label: adobe
description: A natural building material mode from sand, clay, water, and some kind of fibrous or organic material (sticks, straw, and/or manure).

label: alluvial soil
description: Soil which has been eroded and influenced by flowing water and redeposited in a non-marine setting.

label: bagasse
description: The biomass remaining after sugarcane stalks are crushed to extract their juice.

label: oil contaminated soil
description: Soil which has elevated concentrations of oil.

label: clay
description: Particulate environmental material which 1) is composed primarily of clay particles, with only minor proportions of other materials, 2) demonstrates plasticity when wet, and 3) is capable of hardening when dried or fired.

This definition is intentionally ambiguous to support the multiple thresholds set by different authorities.The distinction between silt and clay varies by discipline. Geologists and soil scientists usually consider the separation to occur at a particle size of 2 μm (clays being finer than silts), sedimentologists often use 4–5 μm, and colloid chemists use 1 μm. Geotechnical engineers distinguish between silts and clays based on the plasticity properties of the soil, as measured by the soils' Atterberg limits. ISO 14688 grades clay particles as being smaller than 2 μm and silt particles as being larger. Mixtures of sand, silt and less than 40% clay are called loam. Similar mixtures with greater than 40% clay are often considered clay soils.

label: fuel oil
description: An oil which 1) is liquid at room temperature (approximately 20 degrees Celsius) 2) is intended to be burned in a furnace or boiler for the generation of heat or used in an engine for the generation of power, 3) is obtained from petroleum distillation, either as a distillate or a residue, 4) composed of long hydrocarbon chains, particularly alkanes, cycloalkanes and aromatics.

Oils having a flash point of approximately 42 degrees Celsius and oils burned in cotton or wool-wick burners are not typically considered fuel oils. The term fuel oil is also used in a stricter sense to refer only to the heaviest commercial fuel that can be obtained from crude oil, i.e., heavier than gasoline and naphtha.

label: petroleum
description: A naturally occurring flammable liquid consisting of a complex mixture of hydrocarbons of various molecular weights and other liquid organic compounds, that are found in geologic formations beneath the planetary surfaces.

label: oil
description: A nonpolar, hydrophobic, and lipophilic material which is a viscous liquid at ambient temperatures (about 20 degrees Celsius) or slightly warmer.

label: silage
description: A fermented, high-moisture forage that can be fed to ruminants.

label: animal manure
description: Manure which is derived from the waste products of animals.

label: mushroom compost
description: A compost which generally consists of a combination of wheat straw, dried blood, horse manure and ground chalk, composted together and is the residual compost waste generated by industrial mushroom production.

label: brine
description: It is used (now less popular than historically) to preserve vegetables, fish, and meat.
Water saturated or nearly saturated with salt (NaCl).

label: drinking water
description: Drinking water is water which may be consumed by humans with no adverse effects on their health.

label: metal contaminated soil
description: Soil which has elevated concentrations of metals.

label: enriched soil
description: A portion of enriched soil is a portion of soil with elevated levels of some material entity.
This could be demoted to an inferred class if issues with double inheritance arise.

label: sarcosine enriched soil
description: A portion of sarcosine enriched soil is a portion of soil with elevated levels of sarcosine.

label: trimethylamine enriched soil
description: A portion of trimethylamine enriched soil is a portion of soil with elevated levels of trimethylamine.

label: skatole enriched soil
description: A portion of skatole enriched soil is a portion of soil with elevated levels of skatole.

label: ethanol enriched soil
description: A portion of ethanol enriched soil is a portion of soil with elevated levels of ethanol.

label: acetamide enriched soil
description: A portion of acetamide enriched soil is a portion of soil with elevated levels of acetamide.

label: pantothenate enriched soil
description: A portion of pantothenate enriched soil is a portion of soil with elevated levels of pantothenate.

label: testosterone enriched soil
description: A portion of testosterone enriched soil is a portion of soil with elevated levels of testosterone.

label: kynurenate enriched soil
description: A portion of kynurenate enriched soil is a portion of soil with elevated levels of kynurenate.

label: threonine enriched soil
description: A portion of threonine enriched soil is a portion of soil with elevated levels of threonine.

label: salicylate enriched soil
description: A portion of salicylate enriched soil is a portion of soil with elevated levels of salicylate.

label: poly-beta-hydroxybutyrate enriched soil
description: A portion of poly-beta-hydroxybutyrate enriched soil is a portion of soil with elevated levels of poly-beta-hydroxybutyrate.

label: L-(+)-tartrate enriched soil
description: A portion of L-(+)-tartrate enriched soil is a portion of soil with elevated levels of L-(+)-tartrate.

label: quinate enriched soil
description: A portion of quinate enriched soil is a portion of soil with elevated levels of quinate.

label: pig manure
description: Manure which is primarily composed of pig feces.

label: straw
description: An agricultural byproduct, the dry stalk of a cereal plant, after the nutrient grain or seed has been removed.

label: chalk soil
description: Soil which has increased levels of chalk.

label: scum
description: A layer of impurities that accumulates at the surface of a liquid (especially water or molten metal).

label: travertine
description: Limestone which is deposited from the water of mineral springs or streams saturated with calcium carbonate.

label: foamy environmental material
description: An environmental material which has the quality of a foam.

label: sea foam
description: A foamy environmental material which 1) is created by the agitation of seawater, 2) whose stability depends on the content of the seawater.

The lifetime of sea foam can vary from only seconds to several hours or days. The longer-lasting foam are formed in particular when seawater contain higher concentration of dissolved organic matter that derived from sources such as algal blooms.

label: paddy field soil
description: Soil which is part of a paddy field.

label: alpine soil
description: Soil which is part of an alpine environment.

label: arable soil
description: Soil which is capable of supporting the growth of crops.

label: roadside soil
description: A portion of soil which is found in a roadside area.

label: allotment garden soil
description: Soil which is part of an allotment garden.

label: savanna soil
description: A portion of soil which is found in a savanna.

label: compost soil
description: Soil which is derived from compost.

label: dry soil
description: Soil which has little to no water content and in which minerals and other soluble chemical entities have either bonded or become adsorbed to sold particles due to insufficient water availability.

label: farm soil
description: A portion of soil which is part of a cropland or a rangeland biome.

label: grassland soil
description: A portion of soil which is found in a grassland.

label: jungle soil
description: Soil which is part of a densely forested area subject to tropical climate patterns.

label: sawah soil
description: Soil which is part of a sawah, a wet or irrigated rice field.

label: urea enriched soil
description: A portion of urea enriched soil is a portion of soil with elevated levels of urea.

label: fertilized soil
description: Soil which has been amended with fertilizers.

label: field soil
description: Soil which is part of an agricultural field.

label: lawn soil
description: Soil which is formulated to promote the growth of grasses or other plants used to establish managed areas of vegetation.

label: bacteria enriched soil
description: A portion of bacteria enriched soil is a portion of soil with elevated bacterial abundance.

label: alluvial swamp soil
description: A portion of alluvial soil which is part of a swamp ecosystem.

label: alluvial paddy field soil
description: Alluvial soil whichi is part of a paddy field.

label: burned soil
description: Soil which has been transformed through a combustion process.

label: meadow soil
description: Soil which is part of a meadow.

label: chloropicrin enriched soil
description: A portion of chloropicrin enriched soil is a portion of soil with elevated levels of chloropicrin.

label: humus-rich acidic ash soil
description: Soil which 1) has increased levels of humus, 2) has low pH levels, 3) has increased levels of mineral ash.

label: pond soil
description: Soil which is adjacent to a pond.

label: frozen compost soil
description: Compost soil which is frozen.

label: limed soil
description:
Common liming agents include calcium- and magnesium-rich materials in various forms, including marl, chalk, limestone, burnt lime or hydrated lime. Liming often improves plant growth and increases the activity of soil bacteria, but oversupply may result in harm to plant life.
Liming can also improve aggregate stability on clay soils. For this purpose structure lime, products containing calcium oxide (CaO) or hydroxide (Ca(OH)2) in mixes with calcium carbonate (CaCO3), are often used. Structure liming can reduce losses of clay and nutrients from soil aggregates.
Soil which has been amended with mineral additives to increase its pH.

label: manured soil
description: Soil which has, as a part, a portion of either fresh or processed animal manure.

label: orchid soil
description: Soil which has properties to which plants in the Family Orchidaceae have adapted, including increased levels of aeration and drainage.

label: mountain forest soil
description: Soil which is part of a forest growing on a mountain.

label: beech forest soil
description: Soil which is part of a forest whose communites of arborescent plants are dominated the genus Fagus.

label: muddy soil
description: Soil which is composed of a large proportion of mud, thus having properties resembling mud.

label: orchard soil
description: Soil in which trees from an orchard grow.

label: pasture soil
description: Soil which is found in a pasture and in which vegetation, such as the grass used for the grazing of ungulates, grows.

label: peat soil
description: A histosol which is formed by the decomposition of vegetation or organic matter.

label: salt contaminated soil
description: Soil which has elevated concentrations of sodium chloride.

label: peaty paddy field soil
description: Paddy field soil which has increased levels of peat.

label: steppe soil
description: A portion of soil which is found in a steppe.

label: tropical soil
description: Soil which is part of a tropical environment.

label: vegetable garden soil
description: Garden soil which is part of a garden used for the cultivation of vegetables.

label: greenhouse soil
description: A portion of soil which is found in a greenhouse.

label: heat stressed soil
description: Soil which is has been heated such that its chemical, physical, or biological properties are destabilised.

label: ornithogenic soil
description: Soil which is formed from avian fecal matter.

label: leafy wood soil
description: Soil which is part of a woodland dominated by leafy trees.

label: spruce forest soil
description: Soil which is part of a forest whose communites of arborescent plants are dominated the genus Picea.

label: upland soil
description: Soil which is part of some elevated land.

label: eucalyptus forest soil
description: Soil which is part of a forest whose communites of arborescent plants are dominated the genus Eucalyptus.

label: rubber plantation soil
description: Soil which is part of a rubber plantation.

label: bluegrass field soil
description: Bluegrass field soil is a soil which is found in a field of Kentucky Bluegrass (Poa pratensis).

label: red soil
description:
Red soil typically derives from crystalline rock in warm, temperate, moist climates under deciduous or mixed forest. It has thin organic and organic-mineral layers, a black brown leached layer resting on an illuvium red layer. The majority of red soils have a loamy texture. Their chemical composition varies across regions, but often includes non-soluble material 90.47%, iron 3.61%, aluminium 2.92%, organic matter 1.01%, magnesium 0.70%, lime 0.56%, carbon dioxide 0.30%, potash 0.24%, soda 0.12%, phosphorus 0.09% and nitrogen 0.08%. 

On the uplands, they are thin, poor and gravelly, sandy, or stony and porous, light-colored soils on which food crops like bajra can be grown. In contrast, on the lower plains and valleys they are rich, deep, dark colored fertile loam on which, under irrigation, can produce excellent crops like cotton, wheat, pulses, tobacco, jowar, linseed, millet, potatoes and fruits.

Soil which has 1) low concentrations of nutrients and humus, 2) low water retention capacity, 3) textural variation from sand to clay, 4) a porous and friable structure, and 5) low concentrations of soluble salts.

label: sterile water
description: Sterile water is water which does not contain lliving organisms.

label: underground water
description: This class references any water that's under a planetary surface. For water that is in an aquifer, see "groundwater" (ENVO:01001004). Previously, this class included both.
Water which has physicochemical properties determined by processes which occur beneath the planetary crust.

label: marine mud
description: Mud which is part of a marine ecosystem.

label: lake bottom mud
description: Mud which constitutes the bed of a lake.

label: desert sand
description: Sand which is part of a desert.

label: bulk soil
description: Soil that is not penetrated by the root systems of plants.

label: aerosol
description: Should connect to PATO as "quality of an aerosol"
Airborne solid particles (also called dust or particulate matter (PM)) or liquid droplets.

label: emulsion
description: A mixture of two immiscible (unblendable) substances. One substance (the dispersed phase) is dispersed in the other (the continuous phase).

label: dolomite
description: A sedimentary carbonate rock and a mineral, both composed of calcium magnesium carbonate CaMg(CO3)2 found in crystals.

label: anthropogenic environmental material
description: Anthropogenic material in or on which organisms may live.

label: agricultural environmental material
description: This is quite odd and it probably should be obsoleted. Any material that is a participant in an agricultural process can be seen as an agricultural material.

label: humus
description: Organic matter in soil which has reached a point of stability, where it will break down no further and might, if conditions do not change, remain essentially as it is for centuries, or millennia.

label: mud
description: An environmental material which is a liquid or semi-liquid mixture of water and some combination of soil, silt, and clay particles.

label: silt
description: Particulate environmental material which is primarily composed of silt particles.

This definition is intentionally ambiguous to support the multiple thresholds set by different authorities. Some authorities consider this soil material that contains 80% or more silt and less than 12% clay. In the Udden-Wentworth scale (due to Krumbein), silt particles range between 0.0039 to 0.0625 mm, larger than clay but smaller than sand particles. ISO 14688 grades silts between 0.002 mm and 0.063 mm. In actuality, silt is chemically distinct from clay, and unlike clay, grains of silt are approximately the same size in all dimensions; furthermore, their size ranges overlap. Clays are formed from thin plate-shaped particles held together by electrostatic forces, so present a cohesion. According to the U.S. Department of Agriculture Soil Texture Classification system, the sand-silt distinction is made at the 0.05 mm particle size. The USDA system has been adopted by the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO). In the Unified Soil Classification System (USCS) and the AASHTO Soil Classification system, the sand-silt distinction is made at the 0.075 mm particle size (i.e., material passing the #200 sieve). Silts and clays are distinguished mechanically by their plasticity.

label: sand
description: Particulate environmental material which is composed primarily of particles of sand with only minor proportions of other substances.

This definition is intentionally ambiguous to support the multiple thresholds set by different authorities. Some authorities consider as sands soil material that contains 85% or more sand; the percentage of silt plus 1.5 times the percentage of clay does not exceed 15. coarse sand (sable grossier) 25% or more very coarse and coarse sand, and less than 50% any other one grade of sand.

label: gravel
description: As with all size-based classifications, there is considerable variation in what is considered gravel.
An environmental material which is composed primarily of pieces of gravel.

label: particulate environmental material
description: An environmental material which is composed primarily of particles.

label: planktonic material
description: A portion of planktonic material is a portion of environmental material primarily composed of plankton.

label: terrigenous sediment
description: Sediment comprised of weathered continental rocks, wind blown dust, volcanic ash or other terrestrial material.

label: biogenous sediment
description: Biogenous sediment is derived from living organisms, typically planktonic organisms possessing shells, frustules or coccoliths.

label: hydrogenous sediment
description: Hydrogenous sediment is derived from solutes that precipitate out of sea water by a variety of chemical reactions. These are typically less abundant than other sediment types.

label: cosmogenous sediment
description: Cosmogenous sediment is derived from extraterrestrial dust and debris in the form of meteorites and similar entities.

label: polymetallic nodule
description: Polymetallic nodules, also called manganese nodules, are rock concretions on the sea bottom formed of concentric layers of iron and manganese hydroxides around a core. Nodules vary in size from tiny particles visible only under a microscope to large pellets more than 20 centimetres (8 in) across. However, most nodules are between 5 and 10 cm in diameter.

label: suspended sediment
description: Suspended sediment, or suspended load, is the term for the particles settle  slowly enough to be carried in flowing water (such as a stream or coastal area) either without touching the bed or while only intermittently touching it. These particles are generally of the fine sand, silt and clay size, although larger particles may be carried as well depending on the intensity of the flow.

label: boulder sediment
description: Sediment characterised by an average particle diameter greater than 256 mm.

label: cobble sediment
description: Sediment characterised by an average particle diameter between 64 and 256 mm.

label: pebble sediment
description: Sediment characterised by an average particle diameter between 4 and 32 mm.

label: granular sediment
description: Sediment characterised by an average particle diameter between 2 and 4 mm.

label: sandy sediment
description: Sediment characterised by an average particle diameter between 62.5 micrometers and 2 mm.

label: silty sediment
description: Sediment characterised by an average particle diameter between 3.9 and 62.5 micrometers.

label: clay sediment
description: Sediment characterised by an average particle diameter between 1 and 3.9 micrometers.

label: colloidal sediment
description: Note that by the particle-size-based definition used here, colloidal sediment need not actually be a colloid. If that is the case, please use "suspended colloidal sediment".
Sediment characterised by an average particle diameter below 1 micrometer.

label: mesophilic sediment
description: Sediment characterised by a temperature of 15-45 degrees Celsius and high-to-low oxygenation. Often impacted by hydrothermal fluid flows.

label: thermophilic sediment
description: Sediment characterised by a temperature of 45-75 degrees Celsius and low to no oxygen content. Often impacted by hydrothermal fluid flows.

label: hyperthermophilic sediment
description: Sediment characterised by a temperature of 80-125 degrees Celsius and no oxygen content. Often impacted by hydrothermal fluid flows.

label: hydrothermal fluid
description: High temperature water ejected from hydrothermal vents and laden with dissolved metals and minerals as a result of percolation through crustal rocks.

label: nitrate-reducing sediment
description: Sediment hosting and characterised by active nitrate reducing microbial communities.

label: manganese-reducing sediment
description: Sediment hosting and characterised by active manganese reducing microbial communities.

label: iron-reducing sediment
description: Sediment hosting and characterised by active iron reducing microbial communities.

label: sulphate-reducing sediment
description: Sediment hosting and characterised by active sulphate reducing microbial communities.

label: carbon dioxide-reducing sediment
description: Sediment hosting and characterised by active carbon dioxide reducing microbial communities.

label: organic material
description: Environmental material derived from living organisms and composed primarily of one or more biomacromolecules.

label: biofilm material
description: Material derived from a biofilm, an aggregate of microorganisms in which cells adhere to each other and/or to a surface. These adherent cells are frequently embedded within a self-produced matrix of extracellular polymeric substance (EPS). Biofilm EPS, which is also referred to as slime, is a polymeric conglomeration generally composed of extracellular DNA, proteins, and polysaccharides in various configurations.

label: microbial mat material
description: Material derived from a microbial mat, a multi-layered sheet of micro-organisms, mainly bacteria and archaea. Microbial mats create a wide range of internal chemical environments.

label: marine snow
description: Marine snow is a continuous shower of mostly organic detritus falling from the upper layers of the water column. Its origin lies in activities within the productive photic zone.

label: anoxic water
description: Water which lacks dissolved oxygen.

label: lava
description: Some use 'lava' to refer to rock that is formed when lava cools. This is not the intended meaning of this class. See 'igneous rock' or similar.
Lava is a mixture of molten or semi-molten rock, volatiles, and solids which has extruded beyond a planetary crust.

label: felsic lava
description: Felsic lava is lava which is high in silica (> 69 percent by weight), aluminium, potassium, sodium, and calcium, forming a polymerized liquid rich in feldspar and quartz. Felsic lava has a  higher viscosity than other magma types. Felsic magmas can erupt at temperatures as low as 650 to 750 °C. Unusually hot (>950 °C) rhyolite lavas, however, may flow for distances of many tens of kilometres

label: intermediate lava
description: Intermediate lava is lava which, relative to felsic lava, is lower in aluminium and silica (between 52 and 63 percent by weight), and usually somewhat richer in magnesium and iron. The temperature of intermediate lava ranges from 750 to 950 degrees Celsius, destroying polymerized bonds and promoting more fluid behaviour relative to felsic lavas and also a greater tendency to form phenocrysts. Higher iron and magnesium tends to manifest as a darker groundmass, and also occasionally amphibole or pyroxene phenocrysts.

label: mafic lava
description: Mafic lava generally erupts at temperatures in excess of 950 degrees Celsius. The high temperature and low polymerisation in mafic lava favors low viscosity and chemical diffusion, promoting the formation of large, well-formed phenocrysts.

Mafic lava is lava which, relative to other lava types other than ultramafic lava, has a  high ferromagnesian content and low aluminium and silica content, with silca making up between 45 and 52 percent of its weight.

label: ultramafic lava
description: Ultramafic lava generally erupts at temperatures of 1600 degrees Celsius. Due to its high temperature and composition, the viscosity of ultramafic lava is very low.
Lava which, relative to other lava types, has very high magnesium oxide content and less than 45 percent silica by weight.

label: basalt
description: Basalt is a volcanic rock which is formed by the rapid cooling of basaltic lava.

label: mineral material
description: A mineral material is an environmental material which is primarily composed of some substance that is naturally occurring, solid and stable at room temperature, representable by a chemical formula, usually abiogenic, and that has an ordered atomic structure.

label: water vapour
description: Perhaps a better relation between water vapour and water can be found in or added to RO?
Water vapour is a vapour which is the gas phase of water.

label: atmospheric water vapour
description: Atmospheric water vapour is water vapour that is part of an atmosphere.

label: siltstone
description: A sedimentary rock which is composed mainly of silt. This rock has a grainsize in the silt range, finer than sandstone and coarser than claystones.

label: claystone
description: A clastic sedimentary rock which is composed primarily of clay sized particles.

label: clastic sedimentary rock
description: Clastic sedimentary rocks are sedimentary rocks that are composed of silicate minerals and rock fragments that were transported by moving fluids. Clastic rocks are composed largely of quartz, feldspar, rock (lithic) fragments, clay minerals, and mica; numerous other minerals may be present as accessories and may be important locally.

label: mudstone
description: There is debate on the usage of mudstone and mudrock, and some ambiguity is to be expected. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ The terminology of "mudstone" is not to be confused with the Dunham classification scheme for limestones. In Dunham's classification, a mudstone is any limestone containing less than ten percent carbonate grains. Note, a siliciclastic mudstone does not deal with carbonate grains. Friedman, Sanders, and Kopaska-Merkel (1992) suggest the use of "lime mudstone" to avoid confusion with siliciclastic rocks.
A mudstone is a clastic sedimentary rock which contains a mixture of at least one third of silt- and one third of clay-sized particles.

label: lime mudstone
description: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ The terminology of "mudstone" is not to be confused with the Dunham classification scheme for limestones. In Dunham's classification, a mudstone is any limestone containing less than ten percent carbonate grains. Note, a siliciclastic mudstone does not deal with carbonate grains. Friedman, Sanders, and Kopaska-Merkel (1992) suggest the use of "lime mudstone" to avoid confusion with siliciclastic rocks.
Lime mudstone is a limestone which is primarily composed of either clay-size or both silt-size and clay-size detrital (transported) carbonate grains.

label: slate
description: Slate is a metamorphic rock which is fine-grained, foliated, homogeneous, Slates are derived from clastic sedimentary rocks.

label: water ice
description:
Water ice can appear transparent or opaque bluish-white color, depending on the presence of impurities or air inclusions. The addition of other materials such as soil may further alter its appearance.

When speaking about ice on Earth, usually water ice is meant - the solid, crystalline form of water found in the atmosphere as snow crystals, hail, ice pellets, etc., and on the earth's surface in forms such as hoarfrost, rime, glaze, sea ice, glacier ice, ground ice, frazil, anchor ice, etc.

This form of water is, strictly speaking, called ice Ih, the Roman numeral I distinguishing it from more than a dozen other phases and the letter h distinguishing it from the metastable cubic phase ice Ic. Ice Ih is the only one of the several known phases of water ice that is stable at commonly occurring temperatures and pressures. (Some of the other forms have very unusual properties, ice VII, for example, being stable only at pressures above 22 400 kg/cm^2, but then existing at temperatures up to about 100C.)

It has an open structure with a specific gravity of 0.9166 which is slightly less than water; because the water molecules bond to their neighbors covalently only in four directions; it therefore floats on higher density water, where broken molecular bonds permit closer packing. All commonly occurring forms of ice are crystalline, although large single crystals are relatively rare except in glaciers. The ice crystal lattice possesses hexagonal symmetry that manifests itself in the gross forms of such single crystals as are sometimes found in snow. At an air pressure of one atmosphere, ice melts at 0 C by definition of the Celsius temperature scale. (Strictly speaking the equilibrium point among water, ice, and vapor occurs at +0.01C, the triple point.) On the other hand, ice does not invariably form in liquid water cooled below this temperature; it has a tendency to supercool, more so in the absence of ice nuclei.

In permafrost regions, ice may occupy voids in soils and rocks and may develop in a variety of forms. Ice may be colourless to pale blue or greenish-blue. It may appear white due to included gas bubbles; in exposures, ground ice may also appear black.

In nature ice is formed either by: (a) the freezing of water, (b) the condensation of atmospheric water vapour direct into ice crystals, (c) the compaction of snow with or without the motion of a glacier, or (d) the impregnation of porous snow masses with water which subsequently freeze.
Ice which is formed from water.

label: estuarine water
description: Brackish water which is part of an estuary.

label: root matter
description: An organic material primarily composed of a portion of plant root.
Requested in Issue 115 as part of the annotation of metagenomic submissions present in the European Nucleotide Archive.

label: autoclaved sand
description: Autoclaved sand is sand that has been sterlised by exposure to high pressure saturated steam at at least 121 degrees Celsius.
Requested in Issue 116 as part of the annotation of metagenomic submissions present in the European Nucleotide Archive.

label: granite
description: Requested in issue 45. Some relations to PATO and SWEET classes suggested.
A portion of granite is a portion of igneous  rock which  is intrusive, felsic, granular, and phaneritic.

label: alkaline water
description: A portion of alkaline water is a portion of water with a pH greater than 7.
Here, we commit to a threshold of pH as this is almost universally accepted.

label: acidic water
description: A portion of acidic water is a portion of water with a pH less than 7.

label: agricultural waste material
description: As with other wastes, this is more a role than a material in itself. This should be revised.

Agricultural waste is waste produced as a result of various agricultural operations. It includes manure and other wastes from farms, poultry houses and slaughterhouses; harvest waste; fertilizer run- off from fields; pesticides that enter into water, air or soils; and salt and silt drained from fields.

label: household waste material
description: Household waste refers to waste material usually generated in the residential environment. Waste with similar characteristics may be generated in other economic activities and can thus be treated and disposed of together with household waste.

label: biological waste material
description: Biological waste is waste containing mostly natural organic materials (remains of plants, animal excrement, biological sludge from waste-water treatment plants and so forth).

label: respirable suspended particulate matter
description: A portion of respirable suspended particulate matter is a form of particulate matter composed primarily of solid particles each with a diameter of 10 micrometers or less.

label: snow
description: Snow is an environmental material which is primarily composed of flakes of crystalline water ice.

label: fine respirable suspended particulate matter
description: A portion of fine respirable suspended particulate matter is a form of particulate matter composed primarily of solid particles each with a diameter of 2.5 micrometers or less.

label: ultrafine respirable suspended particulate matter
description: Regulations do not exist for this size class of ambient air pollution particles, which are far smaller than the regulated PM10 and PM2.5 particle classes and are believed to have several more aggressive health implications than those classes of larger particulates.
A portion of fine respirable suspended particulate matter is a form of particulate matter composed primarily of solid particles each with a diameter of  100 nanometers or less.

label: carbon nanotube enriched soil
description: A portion of carbon nanotube enriched soil is a portion of soil with elevated levels of carbon nanotubes.
Logical definition will be created pending import of "carbon nanotube" from CHEBI

label: waterborne particulate matter
description: Particulate environmental material in which small portions of solid material are surrounded by water.

label: andesite
description: In a general sense, it is the intermediate type between basalt and dacite, and ranges from 57 to 63 percent silicon dioxide as illustrated in TAS diagrams. The mineral assemblage is typically dominated by plagioclase plus pyroxene and/or hornblende. Magnetite, zircon, apatite, ilmenite, biotite, and garnet are common accessory minerals. Alkali feldspar may be present in minor amounts.
Andesite is an extrusive igneous, volcanic rock, of intermediate composition, with aphanitic to porphyritic texture.

label: dacite
description: Dacite is an igneous, volcanic rock. It has an aphanitic to porphyritic texture and is intermediate in composition between andesite and rhyolite.  Dacite consists mostly of plagioclase feldspar with biotite, hornblende, and pyroxene (augite and/or enstatite). It has quartz as rounded, corroded phenocrysts, or as an element of the ground-mass. The plagioclase ranges from oligoclase to andesine and labradorite. Sanidine occurs, although in small proportions, in some dacites, and when abundant gives rise to rocks that form transitions to the rhyolites.

label: dacitic lava
description: Rapid solidification of this lava forms dacite.
Lava which is high in silica and low in alkali metal oxides.

label: atmospheric carbon dioxide
description: Atmospheric carbon dioxide is an environmental material composed of carbon dioxide in its gaseous form present in an atmosphere.
This could also be considered a part of an environmental material like air.

label: concrete
description: Missing the class for "aggregate" - tricky to define what it is, exactly. Again, seems more like some sort of material/disposition hybrid.
Concrete is a composite material composed of an aggregate bonded together with a fluid cement which hardens over time.

label: asphalt concrete
description: Asphaltic concrete is a concrete which uses refined asphalt as a cement.

label: asphalt
description: This class refers to naturally-occuring asphalt or bitumen.
Asphalt also known as bitumen is a sticky, black, and highly viscous liquid or semi-solid form of petroleum.

label: refined asphalt
description: Refined asphalt is a sticky, black, and highly viscous liquid or semi-solid with a boiling point above 500 degrees Celsius, obtained from the fractional distillation of crude oil.

label: masonry cement
description: "Cement" refers more to a disposition than a specific material.
Masonry cement is a substance used in construction that has the disposition to set and harden and thus may be used to bind materials together.

label: hydraulic cement
description: Hydraulic cement is a masonry cement which contains activated aluminium silicates or pozzolans, such as fly ash, allowing it to set in wet conditions or underwater.

label: non-hydraulic cement
description: Non-hydraulic cement is a cement which sets by reacting with carbon dioxide in the air and will not set in wet conditions or underwater. It is susceptible to attack by aggresive chemicals after setting.

label: thatch
description:
Some sort of logical definition towards:
composed_primarily_of some ((straw or 'water reed' or rushes or sedge or heather) and has_quality dry)
should be considered, where "rushes", "sedge", etc are represented as materials rather than some sort of taxon.
Thatch is material composed of dry vegetation such as straw, water reed, sedge (Cladium mariscus), rushes, or heather.

label: brick material
description: A portion of brick material is a material derived from a brick which is composed of  kneaded clay-bearing soil, expanded clay aggregate, sand and lime, or concrete that has been fire-hardened or air-dried.

label: plaster
description: Plaster is a building material which has the disposition to harden when it reacts with water, liberating heat through crystallization. Plaster is manufactured as a dry powder and is mixed with water to form a paste when used.

label: gypsum plaster
description: Gypsum plaster is a plaster which is formed by partially dehydrating gypsum by heating it to approximately 150 degrees Celsius and grinding the product into a powder. Gypsum anhydride - formed by heating gypsum above 200 degrees Celsius - may also be used as plaster.

label: lime plaster
description: Lime plaster is a plaster which is primarily composed of calcium hydroxide and an inert filler (such as sand). Coversion of the calcium hydroxide to calcium carbonate through a reaction with carbon dioxide in the air causes the plaster to set.

label: glass
description: This class refers to all forms of glass. For the familiar form present in window panes and drinking glasses, consider silica-based glass.
Glass is an amorphous (non-crystalline) solid which is often transparent.

label: silica-based glass
description: Silica-based glass is a glass composed primarily of silicon dioxide, the primary constituent of sand.
Silica-based glasses are the most common manufactured variety of glass.

label: soda-lime glass
description: Soda-lime glass is a silica-based glass which is composed of approximately 75% silicon dioxide, with sodium oxide and calcium oxide consituting most of its remaining composition.
This type of glass constitutes 90% of manufactured glass.

label: flat glass
description: Most flat glass is soda-lime glass produced by the float glass process. It is more water soluble than container glass.

Flat glass is a soda-lime glass which is composed of approximately 73% silicon dioxide (silica), 14% sodium oxide, 9% calcium oxide, 4% magnesium oxide, 0.15% aluminium oxide, 0.03% potassium oxide, 0.02% titanum dioxide, and 0.01% iron III oxide.

label: container glass
description: Container glass is less water soluble than flat glass.

Container glass is a soda-lime glass which is composed of approximately 74% silicon dioxide (silica), 13% sodium oxide, 10.5% calcium oxide, 1.3% aluminium oxide, 0.3% potassium oxide, 0.2% sulphur trioxide, 0.2% magnesium oxide,  0.04% iron III oxide, and 0.01%  titanum dioxide.

label: quartz glass
description: This is "pure" silica glass. As an ENVO:"environmental material" this class assumes that there remains some possibility that 'contaminants' being present.
Quartz glass is a glass which is composed of silica in amorphous (non-crystalline) form.

label: atmospheric ozone
description: Atmospheric ozone is an environmental material primarily composed of ozone in its gaseous form and present in an atmosphere.

label: paraffin oil
description: A fuel oil which is 1) composed primarily of alkanes having between 5-15 carbon atoms with the general formula CnH2n+2, 2) is generally odorless or has only a slight odor, 3) produces only small amounts of soot relative to other fuel oils, 4) is highly refined.

label: natural gas
description: Natural gas is a hydrocarbon gas mixture consisting primarily of methane, but commonly includes varying amounts of other higher alkanes and sometimes a usually lesser percentage of carbon dioxide, nitrogen, and/or hydrogen sulfide. Natural gas is a fossil fuel formed when layers of buried plants and gases are exposed to intense heat and pressure over thousands of years.

label: liquefied petroleum gas
description: Liquified petroleum gas or liquid petroleum gas (LPG or LP gas), also referred to as simply propane or butane, are flammable mixtures of hydrocarbon gases used as fuel in heating appliances, cooking equipment, and vehicles.

label: hydrocarbon gas
description: A gas that is primarily composed of hydrocarbon molecules.

label: compressed natural gas
description: Compressed natural gas is a natural gas stored at high pressures, typically 20–25 Megapascals.

label: biogas
description: This is distinct from natural gas which is a fossil fuel product.

Biogas is a mixture of different gases produced by the breakdown of organic matter in the absence of oxygen,  is primarily composed of methane and carbon dioxide, and may have small amounts of hydrogen sulfide, water, and siloxanes.

label: liquefied natural gas
description: Liquefied natural gas (LNG) is natural gas (predominantly methane, CH4) that has been converted to liquid form for ease of storage or transport. It takes up about 1/600th the volume of natural gas in the gaseous state. It is odorless, colorless, non-toxic and non-corrosive. LNG achieves a higher reduction in volume than compressed natural gas (CNG) so that the (volumetric) energy density of LNG is 2.4 times greater than that of CNG or 60 percent of that of diesel fuel.

label: compressed biogas
description: Compressed biogas is biogas stored at increased pressures.
This is distinct from compressed natural gas, which refers to the compressed form of a fossil fuel.

label: charcoal
description: Charcoal is a light, black residue, consisting of carbon and any remaining ash, obtained by removing water and other volatile constituents from animal and vegetation substances. Charcoal is usually produced by slow pyrolysis, the heating of wood or other substances in the absence of oxygen.

label: wax
description: A wax is an environmental material which is primarily composed of lipids or other organic compounds that consist of long alkyl chains. Waxes are are malleable near ambient temperatures and melt at approximately 45 degrees Celsius.

label: rainwater
description: Rainwater is liquid water which has precipitated in the form of droplets through the condensation of atmospheric water vapour.

label: plant litter
description: Leaf litter is dead plant material, such as leaves, bark, needles, and twigs, that has fallen to the ground.

label: outer space
description: Outer space is a hard vacuum containing a low density of particles, predominantly a plasma of hydrogen and helium as well as electromagnetic radiation, magnetic fields, neutrinos, dust and cosmic rays that exists between celestial bodies.

label: magma
description: Magma is a mixture of molten or semi-molten rock, volatiles, and solids that is found beneath the uppermost solid layer of a planetary body. Besides molten rock, magma may also contain suspended crystals, dissolved gas and sometimes gas bubbles.

label: tephra
description: Tephra is fragmental material produced by a volcanic eruption regardless of composition, fragment size or emplacement mechanism.

label: tuff
description: Tuff is a type of rock made of volcanic ash ejected from a vent during a volcanic eruption.

label: scoria
description: Scoria differs from pumice in having larger vesicles, thicker vesicle walls and being dark colored and denser.
Scoria is a highly vesicular, dark colored volcanic rock that may or may not contain crystals.

label: pumice
description: Scoria differs from pumice in having larger vesicles, thicker vesicle walls and being dark colored and denser.
Pumice is a volcanic rock that consists of highly vesicular rough textured volcanic glass, which may or may not contain crystals.

label: contaminated air
description: Contaminated air is air which has sufficient concentrations of environmental pollutants such that it may adversely affect a given ecosystem.

label: sodium chloride salt
description: A mineral material composed primarily of sodium chloride.

label: volcanic ash
description: Volcanic ash is an environmental material which consists of fragments of pulverized rock, minerals, and volcanic glass, created during volcanic eruptions and measuring less than 2 millimetres in diameter. Volcanic ash is formed during explosive volcanic eruptions, phreatomagmatic eruptions and during transport in pyroclastic density currents.

label: meltwater
description: Meltwater is the water released by the melting of snow or ice, including glacial ice, tabular icebergs and ice shelves over oceans.

label: bedrock
description: A lithified mass of rock that lies under the loose softer material (regolith) at the surface of the Earth or other terrestrial planet.

label: carbon dioxide emission
description: A volume of carbon dioxide gas emitted by a carbon dioxide emission process.
This is a working definition for #280. Which processes will ultimately be included in the axioms is still open.

label: flame
description: A portion of gas which is emitted by a fire or other exothermic reaction, is of increased temperature, and typically emits light in the visible range.

label: hydrocarbon flame
description: A flame which is produced by the combustion of hydrocarbon fuel.

label: gaseous environmental material
description: A material entity which is composed of one or more chemical entities and has neither independent shape nor volume but tends to expand indefinitely.

label: plasma
description: A material entity which is composed of a volume of unbound positive and negative particles in roughly equal numbers, conducts electricity, and possesses internal magnetic fields.

label: solid environmental material
description: An environmental material which is in a solid state.
This is a defined class: its subclasses will not be asserted, but filled by inference.

label: liquid environmental material
description: An environmental material which is in a liquid state.
This is a defined class: most of its subclasses will not be asserted, but filled by inference.

label: humid air
description: Air which has increased levels of water vapour.

label: water vapour saturated air
description: Air which has a partial pressure of water vapour equal or near equal to its equilibrium vapor pressure at a given temperature.
"Near equal" is meant to reflect that there will be fluctuations around the equilibrium point.

label: smoke
description: Smoke is a collection of airborne solid and liquid particulates and gases emitted when a material undergoes combustion or pyrolysis, together with the quantity of gas that is entrained or otherwise mixed into the mass

label: smog
description: A fog which is intermixed with smoke or other combustion products and their derivatives.

label: fog
description: Fog is more opaque than mist, reducing visibility to under one kilometre. This class refers only to fog formed by materials primarily composed of water. "Fog can be considered a type of low-lying cloud and is heavily influenced by nearby bodies of water, topography, and wind conditions. In turn, fog has affected many human activities, such as shipping, travel, and warfare." https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fog
A visible mass of cloud water droplets or ice crystals suspended in the air at or near the surface of an astronomical body.

label: crystal
description: This class refers to a portion of crystal and not an individual crystal.
A solid material whose constituents, such as atoms, molecules or ions, are arranged in a highly ordered microscopic structure, forming a crystal lattice that extends in all directions.

label: water ice crystal
description: A crystal which is primarily composed of water ice.

Any one of a number of macroscopic, crystalline forms in which ice appears, including hexagonal columns, hexagonal platelets, dendritic crystals, ice needles, and combinations of these forms.  The crystal lattice of ice is hexagonal in its symmetry under most atmospheric conditions.

label: hair ice
description: A type of water ice that forms on dead wood with the assistance of the fungus Exidiopsis effusa and takes the shape of fine, silky hair.

label: clathrate material
description:
This class is not to be confused with CHEBI's "clathrate". The latter refers to the pure substance, while this class refers to clathrates found in nature.
"Traditionally, clathrate compounds are polymeric and completely envelop the guest molecule, but in modern usage clathrates also include host-guest complexes and inclusion compounds." https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clathrate_compound
A material which is primarily composed of a substance arranged as a lattice which can trap or contain other molecules.

label: methane clathrate
description: A clathrate material in which a large amount of methane is trapped within a crystal structure of water, forming a solid similar to ice.

label: marl
description: Marl is a mass of calcium carbonate derived from mollusk shells and mixed with silt and clay.

label: ballast water
description: This definition could be improved, as ballast water is often used in more general ways, beyond the water contained in a ballast tank at any given time. For example, water which has just been released from a ballast tank is often still refered to as ballast water.
Ballast water is water contained in the ballast tanks of sea-going vessels.

label: time crystal
description: While the usage of the term is still debated, the general idea is that time crystals (which have been made using ytterbium ions and defect-bearing diamonds) break temporal symmetry analogously to how mineral crystal break spatial symmetry. While spatial crystals are inhomogeneous in space (vs a gas, which is distributed evenly) due to the ordering of their atoms, the properties of atoms in a time crystal are inhomogeneous in the time dimension.
An open system in non-equilibrium with its environment that exhibits time translation symmetry breaking.

label: fissure water
description: While containment is often enough to classify this subtype of water, it is expected that the water's composition is altered by contact with the solid material bounding the fissure's site.
Water which is partially contained within a fissure or a geological fracture.

label: diatomite
description: A sedimentary rock which is primarily composed of the fossilized, siliceous remains of diatoms mixed with varying amounts of other clays and minerals.

This material is easily crumbled into a fine white to off-white powder. The powder has a particle size ranging from less than 3 micrometres to more than 1 millimetre, but typically 10 to 200 micrometres. The diatoms in each deposit contain different amounts of silica, depending on the age of the deposit. The species of diatom may differ among deposits. The species of diatom is dependent upon the age and paleo-environment of the deposit. In turn, the shape of a diatom is determined by its species. The typical chemical composition of oven-dried diatomaceous earth is 80 to 90% silica, with 2 to 4% alumina (attributed mostly to clay minerals) and 0.5 to 2% iron oxide.

label: industrial wastewater
description: Wastewater which is produced by industrial activity and which contains chemical contaminants other than those associated with urine and fecal matter.

label: groundwater
description: The definition of aquifer is quite permissive, referencing any water bearing rock or unconsolidated material.
Underground water which is located in pore spaces found in rock or unconsolidated deposits such as soil, clay, or gravel.

label: hypereutrophic water
description: The thresholds of eutrophy are fluid and often locally defined.
Water which has a very high concentration of nutrients.

label: sediment permeated by freshwater
description: Sediment which has its porespace filled by water which has very low levels of sodium chloride and/or other salts.

We do not specify numeric thresholds for saline vs. non-saline here, as this is variable. Consider specifying this on the information and/or data layer for your purposes. If you require an ENVO class with a fixed threshold, please request one using our issue tracker.

label: sediment permeated by saline water
description: Sediment which has its porespace filled by water with increased levels of sodium chloride and other salts.

We do not specify numeric thresholds for saline vs. non-saline here, as this is variable. Consider specifying this on the information and/or data layer for your purposes. If you require an ENVO class with a fixed threshold, please request one using our issue tracker.

label: slightly saline water
description: The United States Geological Survey classifies slightly saline water as having around 1,000 to 3,000 ppm (0.1–0.3%) of dissolved salts.
Water which contains a slightly increased concentration of dissolved salts, relative to their concentration in freshwater.

label: moderately saline water
description: The United States Geological Survey classifies moderately saline water as having around 3,000 to 10,000 ppm (0.3–1%) of dissolved salts.
Water which contains a moderately increased concentration of dissolved salts, relative to their concentration in freshwater.

label: highly saline water
description: The United States Geological Survey classifies highly saline water as having around 10,000 to 35,000 ppm (1–3.5%) of dissolved salts.
Water which contains a highly increased concentration of dissolved salts, relative to their concentration in freshwater.

label: mock community culture
description: A cell culture which is composed of a microbial community of known composition.
Mock communities are typically used as positive controls in experiments.

label: single strain cell culture
description: A cell culture which is composed of a single population of bacterial or archaeal cells.

label: oxic water
description: The threshold dissolved oxygen concentration past which water is considered oxic is variable. Typically, this is understood as the concentration at and beyond which organisms inhabiting that water can sustain aerobic metabolism and good health. For most systems, this is above 80% oxygen saturation. Input is welcome here https://github.com/EnvironmentOntology/envo/issues/536
Water which has an appreciable concentration of dissolved oxygen.

label: hypoxic water
description: As with oxic and anoxic water, the thresholds for hypoxia are variable. Typically, a hypoxic state is asserted when dissolved oxygen levels decrease to a level where they have detrimental effects on aerobic aquatic organisms, typically below 30% oxygen saturation.
Water which has low levels of dissolved oxygen.

label: metallic material
description: While this class allows for some degree of contamination by non-metal substances, the material represented should show at least some of the typical features of a pure metal: hardness (except for liquid metals), opacity, lustre, malleability, fusibility, ductile  and good electrical and thermal conductivity.
A material which is composed primarily of one or more pure metals and which shows their properties.

label: aerosolised liquids
description: An aerosol which has non-gaseous parts that are primarily composed of liquid droplets.

label: aerosolised solids
description: An aerosol which has non-gaseous parts that are primarily composed of solid particles.

label: detritus
description: An organic material which is primarily composed of dead particulate matter.

label: forage material
description: Material which is primarily conposed of the vegetation present in tended pastures: mainly grasses, with an interspersion of legumes and other forbs.

label: bovine dairy liquid manure
description: Manure which has been collected directly or indirectly from dairy cattle, as from flushing of manure from concrete feed lanes, free stalls, and milking facilities.

label: poultry manure
description: Manure which is composed primarily of the feces of poultry.

label: heat-treated animal manure
description: Manure which has been subjected to heat treatment for solidification and/or sterilization purposes.

label: composted animal manure
description: Manure which has been subjected to a natural process of 'rotting' or decomposition of its organic matter content by microorganisms under controlled conditions.

label: plant matter
description: Organic material which is primarily composed of plant structures, living or dead.

label: ice
description: An ice is an environmental material which is either frozen or which is maintained in a solid state by gravitational forces or pressure.
Note that ice may be formed at very high temperatures, due to gravitational effects and/or pressure.

label: astrogeological ice
description: This is a term native to the fields of planetary science and astrophysics.  Water, ammonia, and methane are considered "ices" with freezing points of 273 K, 195 K, and 91 K, respectively.
An astrogeological volatile which is composed primarily of chemical compounds with freezing points above an approximate threshold of 100 Kelvin.

label: carbon dioxide ice
description: Ice which is primarily composed of carbon dioxide.

label: methane ice
description: Ice which is primarily composed of methane.

label: ammonia ice
description: Ice which is primarily composed of ammonia.

label: carbon monoxide ice
description: Ice which is primarily composed of carbon monoxide.

label: volatile astrogeological material
description: A material which is composed primarily of chemical elements and compounds with relatively low boiling points, equilibrium condensation temperatures below 1300 Kelvin, and which are part of the crust or atmosphere of a moon or planet.

Examples include nitrogen, water, carbon dioxide, ammonia, hydrogen, methane and sulfur dioxide. In astrogeology, these compounds, in their solid state, often comprise large proportions of the crusts of moons and dwarf planets.

label: astrogeological gas
description: This is a term native to the fields of planetary science and astrophysics.  Hydrogen has a boiling point of 20.271 Kelvin and a melting point of 13.99 Kelvin. Helium has a boiling point of 4.222 Kelvin and a melting point of 0.95 Kelvin.
An astrogeological volatile which is composed primarily of chemical compounds with boiling points around those of hydrogen and helium.

label: refractory astrogeological material
description: A material which is composed primarily of chemical elements and compounds which have equilibrium condensation temperatures above approximately 1300 Kelvin and which are part of the crust or atmosphere of a moon or planet.
The refractory group includes elements and compounds like metals and silicates (commonly termed rocks) which make up the bulk of the mass of the terrestrial planets and asteroids in the inner belt.

label: acidic soil
description: Soil which has increased levels of molecules or ions capable of donating a hydron (proton or hydrogen ion) to other chemical entities, or, alternatively, capable of forming covalent bonds with other chemicals via the acceptance of an electron pair, resulting in a bulk pH measurement of less than 7.

label: acidic volcanic ash
description: Volcanic ash which has increased levels of molecules or ions capable of donating a hydron (proton or hydrogen ion) to other chemical entities, or, alternatively, capable of forming covalent bonds with other chemicals via the acceptance of an electron pair, resulting in a bulk pH measurement of less than 7.

label: algal material
description: An organic material which is primarily composed of living or dead algae, along with their exudates.

label: brown sea ice
description: Sea ice which has a brown colouration, either due to 1) the presence of pigments which are or were contained in the members of ecological assemblages, such as algal communities, living or trapped within the ice or 2) due to the presence of trapped sediments.

label: alluvium
description: Soil or sediment which has been eroded and influenced by flowing water and redeposited in a non-marine setting.

label: alluvial sediment
description: Sediment which has been transported by flowing water and redeposited in a non-marine setting.

label: alluvial deposit
description: A rock which is formed as a result of the lithification of alluvium.

label: kerogen
description: Organic material which is in a solid phase and contained in sedimentary rock.

label: sapropelic kerogen
description: Kerogen which cotains alginite, amorphous organic matter, cyanobacteria, freshwater algae, and land plant resins, thus having a hydrogen to carbon ratio above 1.25, and oxygen to carbon ratio below 0.15, readily produces liquid hydrocarbons, has reduced concentrations of aromatic structures, and primarily derived from proteins and lipids.

label: labile kerogen
description: Kerogen from which heavy hydrocarbons (such as oils) are derived following chemical break down.

label: recalcitrant kerogen
description: Kerogen from which light hydrocarbons (such as hydrocarbon gases) are derived following chemical break down.

label: planktonic kerogen
description: Kerogen which is enriched in sulfur compounds, has a hydrogen to carbon ratio under 1.25, an oxygen to carbon ratio between 0.03 and 0.18, derives into mixtures of hydrocarbon gas and oil, and derives from marine organic materials (primarily lipids) which are formed in reducing environments.

label: sulfrous kerogen
description: Planktonic kerogen which has high concentrations of sulfur compounds.

label: humic kerogen
description: Kerogen which derives from land plants, resembles wood or coral in structure, has a hydrogen to carbon ratio under 1, an oxygen to carbon ratio between 0.03 to 0.3, and which primarily produces coal or hydrocarbon gas on degradation.

label: residual kerogen
description: Kerogen which has a hydrogen to carbon ratio less than  0.5 and primarily composed of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons.

label: saline shrimp pond water
description: Saline water which is derived from sea water and used during the cultivation of crustaceans.

label: vog
description: A fog which is composed of liquid aerosols and gases derived from volcanic gas emissions (primarily sulfur oxides), formed when sulfur-bearing gases react with sunlight, oxygen, and moisture in an atmosphere.

"Vog and smog are different. Vog is formed when sulfur oxides emitted by a volcano react with moisture to form an aerosol. The aerosol scatters light, thus making the vog visible. Smog is formed largely from the incomplete combustion of fuel, reacting with nitrogen oxides and ozone produced from carbon monoxide by reactions with sunlight. The result is also a visible aerosol."

label: stormwater
description: Water which accumulates on a solid surface during precipitation events and snow/ice melt.
"Stormwater can soak into the soil (infiltrate), be held on the surface and evaporate, or runoff and end up in nearby streams, rivers, or other water bodies (surface water)."

label: urban stormwater
description: Stormwater which accumulates in an urban ecosystem.
"Stormwater can soak into the soil (infiltrate), be held on the surface and evaporate, or runoff and end up in nearby streams, rivers, or other water bodies (surface water)."

label: rural stormwater

"Stormwater can soak into the soil (infiltrate), be held on the surface and evaporate, or runoff and end up in nearby streams, rivers, or other water bodies (surface water)."

label: barium dust

label: slate dust

label: kaolin dust

description: An organic environmental material which is primarily composed of gill tissue.

description: Gill tissue material which is part of salt-water mussel in the family Mytilidae

label: Bathymodiolus gill tissue material

label: necromass
description: Biomass which is composed primarily of dead organisms, their parts, or their organic derivatives.

label: abyssal clay
description: Clay which is part of an abyssal plain.

label: ultisol
description: A soil which has high mineral content and which contain no calcareous material, have less than 10% weatherable minerals its surface layer, and have less than 35% base saturation throughout its volume.

The word "ultisol" is derived from "ultimate", because ultisols were seen as the ultimate product of continuous weathering of minerals in a humid, temperate climate without new soil formation via glaciation.

label: haze
description: An aersolised mass of dust, smoke, or other dry particulates which scatters visible light thus obsscuring visibility through an atmosphere.

label: mist
description: This class refers only to mist formed by materials primarily composed of water. Mist is less dense than fog, and visibility is typically greater than one kilometre.
A visible mass of water droplets or ice crystals suspended in the air at or near a planetary surface, formed when humid air cools rapidly.

label: freshwater ice
description: Water ice which is formed by the freezing of fresh water.

label: congelation sea ice
description: Congelation ice usually forms through the fusion/coalescence of platelets into solid ice.
Sea ice which 1) has formed on the submerged surface (i.e. the base) of an existing mass of sea ice and 2) is composed of columnar crystals due to the downward growth of the crystals into the water.

label: permafrost congelation ice
description: Water ice which has formed in a mass of permafrost.

label: congelation ice in a fresh water body
description: Freshwater ice which forms downward from the surface of a freshwater water body and is transparent due to a reduced number of air bubbles trapped in its mass.

label: freshwater congelation ice
description: Freshwater ice which forms on a solid substrate through the freezing of freshwater.

label: ice cave congelation ice
description: Freshwater congelation ice which has formed on a solid substrate in an ice cave.

label: frazil
description: Small, needle-like (spicules), plate-like, or discoid crystals derived from nearly pure fresh water, suspended in a water body.

Typically 3 to 4 millimeters in diameter. These may form in both marine water and fresh water. They represent the first stages of sea ice growth; they merge under calm conditions to form thin sheets of ice on the surface (frazil ice), and consist of nearly pure fresh water. In fresh water, they form in supercooled water that is too turbulent to permit coagulation into sheet ice.  This is most common in swiftly flowing streams. They may accumulate as anchor ice on submerged objects obstructing the water flow.

label: hard-frozen soil
description: Frozen soil which is firmly cemented by water ice, is subject to brittle failure, and exhibits practically no consolidation under load.

label: frozen soil
description: Soil which is below the freezing point of water.

label: plastic-frozen soil
description: Frozen soil which is cemented by water ice but has viscous properties due to its high, unfrozen water content and therefore will compress and deform under load.

label: friable-frozen soil
description: Frozen soil which has very low total water content and is not cemented by ice; its compressibility is the same as that of unfrozen soils having the same composition, total water content and density.

label: water-body-derived ice
description: Ice which has formed as the result of freezing of water which was part of a water body.
In the United States, NOAA considers ice formed from the freezing of the waters of the Great Lakes as being the same as sea ice. This class attempts to provide a distinction for clarity.

label: colloidal suspension

An environmental material which is primarily composed of a dispersed phase of insoluable particles, approximately between 1 nanometer and 1 micrometer in maximum dimension, distributed throughout a material acting as a medium of suspension.

label: gel
description: An environmental material which is solid, jelly-like, and exhibits no flow when in steady state material and which contains liquid dispersed in and held in place by cross-linked structures of a solid medium.

label: hydrogel
description: A gel which is primarily composed of a network of polymer chains that are hydrophilic, sometimes found as a colloidal gel in which water is the dispersion medium.

label: quicksand
description: Particulate environmental material which 1) is primarily composed of a fine, granular material such as sand, silt, or clay suspended in and saturated by water and 2) readily liquefies when weight is applied, losing strength and permitting objects to sink until their weight and buoyancy offset the weight of the displaced quicksand.

label: kerosene oil
description: For speakers of British English, kerosene is often referred to as paraffin.
A fuel oil which 1) is derived from petroleum oil, 2) has a strong odor, 3) produces large quantities of soot relative to other fuel oils, 4) is less refined than fuel oils such as paraffin.

label: ice-bearing permafrost

label: atmospheric aerosol

label: hydrothermally-influenced sediment

label: volcanic soil

label: hoar
description: Frost which is composed of interlocking ice crystals formed by vapour transfer (sublimation followed by deposition) of water vapour on some surface.

label: depth hoar
description: Depth hoar is associated with very fast crystal growth under large temperature gradients. Sometimes a layer of depth hoar forms just above, and may assist in identifying the summer surface. The low density and low strength of depth hoar can make it difficult to retrieve unbroken core sections during coring, and can complicate estimates of accumulation by microwave remote sensing. Layers of depth hoar also increase the likelihood of avalanching. This is one way in which firn formation may begin. Depth hoar is similar in physical origin to crevasse hoar.
Hoar which is usually cup-shaped and facetted and which forms within dry, low-density snow beneath the snow surface.

label: rime
description: Rime is denser and harder than hoarfrost, but lighter, softer, and less transparent than glaze. Rime is composed essentially of discrete ice granules and has densities as low as 0.2-0.3 g cm-3. Glaze is generally continuous but with some air pockets and has much higher densities. Factors that favor rime formation are small drop size, slow accretion, a high degree of supercooling, and rapid dissipation of latent heat of fusion. The opposite effects favor glaze formation. Both rime and glaze occur when supercooled water drops strike an object at a temperature below freezing. Such formation on terrestrial objects constitutes an ice storm; on aircraft, it is called aircraft icing (where rime is known as rime ice). Either rime or glaze may form on snow crystals, droxtals, or other ice particles in the atmosphere. When such a deposit is wholly or chiefly of rime, snow pellets result; when most or all of the deposit is glaze, ordinary hail or ice pellets result. The alternating clear and opaque layers of some hailstones represent glaze and rime, deposited under varying conditions around the growing hailstone.

Water ice which 1) has a white or milky and opaque appearance, 2) has a granular texture, and 3) is formed as a result of the deposition and rapid freezing of supercooled water drops as they make contact with an exposed object.

label: frost
description: In British usage, a day on which the minimum temperature at the level of the ground or on the tops of low, close-growing vegetation falls to -0.9C (30.4F) or below (also called a "day with ground frost").  In more general usage, "frost" can refer to the condition that exists when the temperature of the Earth's surface and Earthbound objects fall below the melting point of water (0 degrees Celsius or 32 degrees Fahrenheit). Depending upon the actual values of ambient-air temperature, dewpoint, and the temperature attained by surface objects, frost may occur in a variety of forms. These include a general freeze, hoarfrost (or white frost), and dry freeze (or black frost). If a frost period is sufficiently severe to end the growing season (or delay its beginning), it is commonly referred to as a killing frost.
An environmental material which is primarily composed of minute ice crystals forming a fuzzy layer over a cold surface by direct deposition of water vapor.

label: fracking liquid
description: A liquid environmental material which is composed primarily of water ammended with thickening agents and proppants.

label: graupel
description: Often indistinguishable from very small soft hail except for the size convention that hail must have a diameter greater than 5 mm. Sometimes distinguished by shape into conical, hexagonal, and lump (irregular) graupel.
Snow which is composed of heavily rimed particles typically 2 to 5 millimeters in diameter (0.1 to 0.2 inch).

label: surface hoar
description: When buried by snowfall, surface hoar may be considered depth hoar. The crystals formed by surface hoar are usually leaf-, fern- or plate-shaped and facetted. Two types of surface hoar are the fernlike ice crystals deposited directly on a snow surface and the hoarfrost that has grown primarily in two dimensions, as on a window or other smooth surface.
Hoar which a) forms on surfaces, b) occurs when the temperature of the surface is colder than the air above and colder than the frost point of that air.

label: hoar crystal
description: A water ice crystal which is a part of a deposit of hoarfrost and which only grows by desublimation.

The adult will use the material to form a protective structure to house and raise their young. Nests are built primarily by birds, but also by mammals, fish, insects and reptiles.
