description: Red clay, also known as pelagic clay, accumulates in the deepest and most remote areas of the ocean. Containing less than 30% biogenic material, its composition is a varied mix of very fine quartz and clay minerals, authigenic deposits precipitated directly from seawater, and micrometeorites. Though called "red" because it sometimes takes the color of oxidized iron minerals, it is usually brownish in color. Its ultimate origin is uncertain, but red clay seems to be mostly derived from distant rivers, and windblown dust. Covering 38% of the ocean floor, it accumulates more slowly than any other sediment type, at only 0.1-0.5 cm / 1000 yr.

label: calcareous ooze
description: Calcareous ooze is a marine sediment composed primarily of the shells--also known as tests--of foraminifera, coccolithophores, and pteropods. This is the most common pelagic sediment by area, covering 48% of the world ocean's floor. This type of ooze is limited to depths above the Carbonate Compensation Depth at time of burial. It accumulates more rapidly than any other pelagic sediment type, with a rate that varies from 0.3 - 5 cm / 1000 yr.

label: animal feed
description: Most animal feed is from plants but some is of animal origin. Fodder refers particularly to food given to the animals (including plants cut and carried to them), rather than that which they forage for themselves. It includes hay, straw, silage, compressed and pelleted feeds, oils and mixed rations, and also sprouted grains and legumes.
Food material which can be used to meet nutritional requirements of animals, particularly livestock such as cattle, goats, sheep, horses, chickens and pigs.

label: contaminated animal feed
description: Contaminated animal feed is an animal feed that has become contaminated with or come contact with microorganisms or toxic chemicals.

label: hide
description: A skin obtained from animals for human use typically from deer or cattle sources used to produce leather, shoes, fashion accessories, musical instruments.

label: bone meal
description: A mixture of crushed and coarsely ground bones that is used as an organic fertilizer for plants and formerly in animal feed.

label: plant feed
description: Food material which can be used to meet nutritional requirements of plants.

label: surface soil
description: A soil consisting of the upper layer of soil on the surface consisting of loose material capable of supporting life composed of a mixture of mineral and organic matter.

label: ash
description: An environmental material that is the non-aqueous, non-gaseous residues that remain after something is burned.

label: coal
description: A combustible black or brownish-black sedimentary rock usually occurring in rock strata in layers or veins called coal beds or coal seams.

label: ore
description: a type of rock that contains sufficient minerals with important elements including metals that can be economically extracted from the rock.

label: uranium ore
description: Ore which contains uranium.
The primary uranium ore mineral is uraninite

label: coal dust
description: Dust which is derived from coal.

label: mineral dust
description: Dust which is derived from mineral material.

label: fibrous dust
description: Dust which is composed of fibrous material.

label: metallic dust
description: Dust which is composed primarily of some metallic material.

label: clay dust
description: Dust which is derived from clay material.

label: asbestos dust
description: Dust which is derived from asbestos

label: grain dust
description: Dust that comes from grain and all the other substances associated with its cultivation & harvesting.

label: fume
description: A gas, smoke, or vapor that smells strongly or is dangerous to inhale.

label: vanadium fume
description: Respirable vapor of vanadium.

label: natural wax
description: A wax that is naturally synthesized by a plant or animal.

label: paraffin wax
description: A white or colourless soft solid derivable from petroleum, coal or oil shale, that consists of a mixture of hydrocarbon molecules containing between twenty and forty carbon atoms.

label: oil shale
description: An organic-rich fine-grained sedimentary rock containing kerogen from which liquid hydrocarbons called shale oil can be produced.

label: paint
description: Any liquid, liquefiable, or mastic composition that, after application to a substrate in a thin layer, converts to a solid film. It is most commonly used to protect, color, or provide texture to objects.

label: lead paint
description: Paint that contains lead.

label: wood ash
description: the residue powder that is derived from the combustion of wood.

label: coal ash
description: Ash that is produced from the burning of coal.

label: fly ash
description: A very fine, powdery material composed mostly of silica made from the burning of finely ground coal in a boiler.

label: bottom ash
description: a coarse, angular ash particle that is too large to be carried up into the smoke stacks so it forms in the bottom of the coal furnace.

label: boiler slag
description: molten bottom ash from slag tap and cyclone type furnaces that turns into pellets that have a smooth glassy appearance after it is cooled with water.

label: flue gas desulfurization material
description: a material leftover from the process of reducing sulfur dioxide emissions from a coal-fired boiler that can be a wet sludge consisting of calcium sulfite or calcium sulfate or a dry powered material that is a mixture of sulfites and sulfates.

label: mangrove biome soil
description: Mangrove soils are typically saline, anoxic, acidic and frequently waterlogged.
Soil which is located in a mangrove biome.

label: fluid environmental material
description: An environmental material which is unable to resist shear forces and continuously deforms when subject to them.

label: neve
description: Névé that survives a full season of ablation turns into firn.
Partially compacted granular snow, which has undergone several cycles of melting and refreezing while being compacted, usually found on the atmosphere-exposed surface of a glacier.

label: firn
description: Firn derives from névé which has survived a full season of ablation and has undergone a metamorphic transition.

Granular snow which contains a proportion of fused granules formed through melting and re-thawing while being compacted by the weight of overlying material and which contains interconnected gaseous pores.

label: glacial ice
description: Any water ice that is part of a glacier.

label: erosionally enriched glacial ice
description: Glacial ice which contains material liberated during a glacial erosion process.

label: blue ice
description: The blue 'appearance' is to be understood as that within the visual range of humans.
Water ice containing little to no air bubbles resulting in a reduction of internal light scattering and, given sufficient volume, a blue appearance.

label: soot
description: Particulate environmental material which is composed primarily of carbon particles formed through the incomplete combustion of hydrocarbons.

label: erosionally enriched ice
description: Water ice which contains material liberated during an erosion process.

label: powdery snow
description: Described as having a fluffy appearance.
Uncompacted snow containing trapped atmospheric gases.

label: marine sediment
description: Particles of marine sediment are primarily generated by 1) processes in terrestrial systems and transported to the marine realm by the action of rivers or aeolian processes (amongst other routes) , 2) marine organisms, 3) chemical processes in seawater, or 4) cosmogeneous input.
Sediment which has been transported through the marine water column, settling on the seafloor.

label: shallow marine sediment
description: Marine sediment soured from either terrestrial systems, marine organisms, seawater and or cosmogeneous sources, which is transported through the marine water column, and accumulates within shallow regions of the oceanic basin close to continents, such as the continental shelf, or continental slope.

label: cryoconite deposit
description: Particulate environmental material which is composed primarily of dust, rock, and soot, as well as the microbial communities associated with these materials, deposited on an ice mass by an aeolian process.

label: frazil ice
description: Typically 3 to 4 millimeters in diameter. These new ice classes refer to both marine water and fresh water ice. If using this term for annotation, use it in conjunction with another envo term to express whether the ice is in a marine, freshwater, or other system.
New ice which is composed frazil which has congealed into a thin sheet.

label: new ice
description: sea ice types include frazil, grease ice, slush, and shuga. These new ice classes refer to both marine water and fresh water ice. If using this term for annotation, use it in conjunction with another envo term to express whether the ice is in a marine, freshwater, or other system.
Water ice which is formed from freezing water and is suspended in a water body.

label: first year ice
description: Sea ice develops from young ice; thickness from 0.3 to 2 meters (1 to 6.6 feet).  Sea ice be subdivided into thin first-year ice (white ice), medium first-year ice, and thick first-year ice.  First-year ice is distinguished from older ice primarily by having a higher salinity. Undeformed first-year ice differs from older ice in that it is smoother and lacks refrozen melt ponds. Characteristically level where undisturbed by pressure, but where ridges occur, they  distinguished by being larger, more angular, and more porous than multiyear ridges.
Sea ice which has formed over a single freezing season.

label: second year ice
description: Sea ice which is thicker than first year ice, and has survived a seasonal melting process.

label: multiyear ice
description: Sea ice which is thicker than second year ice, and has survived more than two seasonal melting process.

label: shuga
description: These new ice classes refer to both marine water and fresh water ice. If using this term for annotation, use it in conjunction with another envo term to express whether the ice is in a marine, freshwater, or other system.
New ice, which is spongy, lumpy and opaque, and forms from water which freezes in an agitated water body.

label: slush ice
description: These new ice classes refer to both marine water and fresh water ice. If using this term for annotation, use it in conjunction with another envo term to express whether the ice is in a marine, freshwater, or other system.
A slurry of frazil, snow, and liquid water.

label: methane-laden permafrost
description: Other hydrocarbon gasses such as carbon dioxide may also be present. These pockets can be sufficently large that the permafrost surface will undulate when pressure is applied.
Permafrost which contains pockets of trapped methane gas.

label: slab snow
description: Snow which is cohesive, hard and overlies weaker snow.

label: agricultural potting mixture
description: An agricultural environmental material which 1) is composed of a mixture of materials such as peat, composted bark, sand, perlite, or compost, and 2) serves as a medium in which to grow plants.

label: freezing fog
description: A fog the droplets of which freeze upon contact with exposed objects, forming a coating of rime or glaze.

label: ice fog
description: Fog which is composed of particles of ice.

The suspended particles may be partly ice crystals 20 to 100 micron in diameter, but chiefly, especially when dense, droxtals 12-20 micron in diameter. Ice fog is formed by direct freezing of supercooled water droplets with little growth directly from the vapor. It occurs at very low temperatures, and usually in clear, calm weather in high latitudes. The sun is usually visible and may cause halo phenomena or luminous pillars. Ice fog is rare at temperatures warmer than -30 °C, and increases in frequency with decreasing temperature until it is almost always present at air temperatures of -45 °C in the vicinity of a source of water vapor. Such sources are the open water of fast-flowing streams or of the sea, herds of animals, volcanoes, and especially products of combustion for heating or propulsion. At temperatures warmer than -30 °C, these sources can cause steam fog of liquid water droplets, which may turn into ice fog when cooled.

label: chicken manure
description: Poultry manure made of chicken feces.

label: gypsum
description: A soft sulfate mineral composed of calcium sulfate dihydrate.

label: litter
description: Environmental material consisting of waste products that have been discarded at an unsuitable location.

label: manure
description: Most manure consists of animal feces; other sources include compost and green manure.
An environmental material consisting of organic matter from plants and/or animals that is used in agriculture as fertilizer.

label: cork
description: Plant matter consisting of an impermeable buoyant material, the phellem layer of bark tissue.

label: natural-based polymer
description: Macromolecules that are obtained naturally from plants or animals.

label: cellophane
description: Cellophane is used for food packaging.
A thin, transparent sheet made of regenerated cellulose.

label: pliofilm
description: Synthetic plastic which is composed of a glossy, moistureproof membrane made of rubber hydrochloride.

label: mylar
description: A polyester film made from stretched polyethylene terephthalate (PET).

label: ceramic
description: A solid environmental material that is hard, brittle, heat-resistant and corrosion-resistant, made by shaping and then firing a nonmetallic mineral at a high temperature.

label: latex
description: Latex is made by some plants, but synthetic latexes can be manufactured as well.
A stable dispersion (emulsion) of polymer microparticles in an aqueous medium.
synonyms: Natural rubber, India rubber, Gum elastic, Non-vulcanized rubber

label: stagnant water
description: A liquid water which has no current or flow and is susceptible to contamination by pathogens or pathogenic vectors.

label: wood dust
description: Dust which is 1) generated when wood is processed and 2) composed primarily of cellulose, polyoses, and lignin.

Wood dust is typically generated through processes where wood is chipped, sawed, turned, drilled or sanded. The chemical composition of wood dust depends on the species of tree. Wood dust is not typically produced for specific uses. However, it is used commercially for wood composts. The primary routes of potential human exposure to wood dust are inhalation and dermal contact. It is known to be a human carcinogen.

label: diesel fuel
description: A liquid fuel used in diesel engines, whose fuel ignition takes place, without any spark, as a result of compression of the inlet air mixture and then injection of fuel.

label: gasoline
description: Gasoline consists mostly of organic compounds obtained by the fractional distillation of petroleum, enhanced with a variety of additives.
A clear petroleum-derived flammable liquid which is used as fuel in most spark-ignited internal combustion engines.

label: diesel exhaust
description: A gas which results from the incomplete or complete combustion of diesel fuel.

label: gasoline exhaust
description: A gas which results from the complete or incomplete combustion of gasoline fuel.

label: xanthan gum
description: A polysaccharide that functions as an emulsifier, stabilizer, and thickener in mixtures.

label: tragacanth
description: A naturally occurring plant-based gum, which functions as a viscous, odorless, tasteless, water-soluble mixture of polysaccharides that absorbs water to become a gel/paste.
Tragacanth has many uses, including as an emulsifier, thickener, stabilizer, and texturant additive for foods, pharmaceuticals, and art materials.

label: resin
description: A solid or highly viscous plant or synthetic based substance that is typically convertible into polymers.

label: shellac
description: A resin secreted by the female lac bug, which is dissolved in alcohol to be used as a brush-on colorant, food glaze, and wood finish.

label: primer (paint)
description: A paint product which adheres to surfaces and forms a binding layer, preparing it to receive paint.

label: oil-based paint
description: A slow-drying paint that consists of particles of pigment suspended in a drying oil, commonly linseed oil.

label: acrylic paint
description: A water soluble, fast-drying paint made of pigment suspended in acrylic polymer emulsion.

label: luminescent paint
description: A paint that exhibits luminescence, giving off visible light through fluorescence, phosphorescence, or radioluminescence.

label: rock dust
description: Rock dust is widely used in mining to prevent coal dust explosions, or in agriculture for organic farming uses.
Dust which is composed of minerals and trace elements, generated by  finely crushed rock.

label: radioactive material
description: Any material containing unstable atoms that emit ionizing radiation as it decays.

label: volume of cyanoacrylate
description: Cyanoacrylates have industrial, medical, and household uses. A strong fast-acting adhesive which is an ester of cyanoacrylic acid.
An environmental material which is primarily composed of cyanoacrolate.

label: rubber cement
description: An environmental material which is composed of elastic polymers mixed in a solvent.
Solvents typically used include acetone, hexane, heptane or toluene.

label: methyl cellulose paste
description: An environmental material which is 1) composed primarily of methyl cellulose and water, and 2) formulated to fix wallpaper to walls.

label: permanent hair dye
description: An environmental material which is 1) manufactured and 2) primarily composed of hydrogen peroxide and ammonia, and 3) when applied to hair, can alter the natural hair pigments for 6-8 weeks.

label: pharmaceutical ink
description: A colorant fluid which is 1) manufactured and 2) composed of alcohol, titanium dioxide, and propylene glycol.

label: gel ink
description: A colorant fluid which is 1) manufactured and 2) composed of copper phthalocyanine, iron oxides, water, and biopolymers.

label: soy ink
description: A colorant fluid which is 1) manufactured and 2) primarily composed of soybean oil, as well as pigment, resin, and wax.

label: aqueous inkjet printer ink
description: A colorant fluid which is 1) manufactured, 2) primarily composed of water, as well as glycol, and dye, and 3) intended for use in inkjet printers.

label: emissions from petroleum combustion
description: An environmental material which is composed primarily of gases and particles produced by the combustion of petroleum fuels.

label: colorant fluid
description: A liquid environmental material which 1) contains at least one substance which can act as a chemical colorant.

label: toxic waste
description: Waste which contains toxic components (e.g., heavy metals or radiation) which can cause harm to organisms and/or the environment.

label: snow crystal
description: A water ice crystal which is constituted by water molecules aligned in a hexagonal array.

label: chemically contaminated sediment
description: Sediment which contains some chemical contaminant.

label: cooling water
description: Cooling water is commonly used for cooling automobile internal combustion engines and power stations.
Liquid water which is a participant in a water cooling process.

label: food waste
description: A waste material which is primarily composed of uneaten food and removed from the food supply chain.
The causes of food waste or loss are numerous and can occur during production, processing, distribution, retail and consumption.

label: formation fluid
description: A fluid environmental material which is contained in geologic formations naturally.

label: interstitial water
description: Liquid water which occurs naturally within the pores of rocks and sediments.

label: bituminous sand
description: An environmental material which consists of either loose sands or partially consolidated sandstone, containing a naturally occurring mixture of sand, clay, and water, soaked with a dense and extremely viscous form of petroleum.

label: saprolite
description: Rock which is derived from bedrock through chemical weathering

label: slurry
description: An environmental material which is composed of insoluble solid particles suspended in a liquid.

label: pathogen-suppressive soil
description: The pathogenicity that is suppressed is typically directed towards plants, especially crops. Soils are typically classified as pathogen-suppressive if a pathogen 1) cannot establish itself or persist, 2) is able to establish itself, but causes little or no damage, or 3) is able to establishe itself, but only causes disease that does not result in long-term harm.
Soil which has properties that restrict a pathogen's ability to establish itself, persist, or cause disease that results in long-term harm.

label: marine lake water
description: Liquid water which is either part of or was removed from a marine lake.

label: microbialite
description: A sedimentary rock which is made of carbonate mud whose formation is mediated by microbes in the benthic zone.

label: spring water
description: Water which comes from a spring.

label: cloud water
description: Fresh water which is harvested from cloud.

label: crustal fluid
description: The presence or absence of fluids exerts a fundamental control on rheology.
Fluid environmental material which is present in the continental crust and dictates the nature and extent of crustal deformation.

label: lichen material
description: An organic material which is derived from lichen mats.

label: periphytic biofilm
description: Periphytic biofilm coats the submerged surfaces in most bodies of water
Biofilm consisting of a mixture of algae, cyanobacteria, microbes, and detritus.

label: epilithon
description: Periphyton colonizing rock substrata

label: epipelon
description: Periphyton colonizing silt substrata

label: epiphyton
description: Periphyton colonizing surface of aquatic plants

label: epipsammon
description: Periphyton colonizing sand substrata

label: epixylon
description: Periphyton colonizing woody substrata

label: stream water
description: Water which is part of a stream.

label: lake water
description: Water which is part of a lake.

label: soil organic matter
description: Organic material in soil, which consists of plant and animal residues at various stages of decomposition, cells and tissues of soil organisms, and substances synthesized by soil organisms.

label: particulate organic matter
description: Particulate environmental material which is composed primarily of organic material.

label: particulate organic carbon
description: Particulate organic matter which is composed primarily of carbon.

label: particulate organic nitrogen
description: Particulate organic matter which is composed primarily of nitrogen.

label: thermoplastic material
description: An environmental material which is capable of, repeatedly, becoming plastic when heated and hardening again when cooled.

label: foamed plastic
description: A plastic which has a matrix- or sponge-like structure with numerous, hollow internal spaces.

label: plastic
description: "High molecular mass" can be ambiguous as it does not set a threshold for what is considered "high". Here we make no commitment to a threshold.
An environnmental material which 1) is composed primarily of polymers with high molecular mass and 2) once deformed does not spontaneously return to its original shape.

label: natural plastic
description: Plastic which is composed primarily of polymers produced by processes whose agents do not include humans or their technologies.

label: synthetic plastic
description: A plastic which is composed primarily of polymers produced by a manufacturing process.

label: compacted soil
description: A soil which has a high bulk density and/or a low porosity. A compacted soil has a reduced rate of both water infiltration and drainage

label: runoff
description: Runoff often gathers debris and solutes from the materials it flows over or through, and often flows into a water body.
Liquid water which 1) flows over land and 2) is not absorbed or retained by the materials if flows over or through.

label: residual water in soil
description: Liquid water which is present in soils as discontinuous volumnes of water in contact with solid and gaseous components of the soil.

label: treated wastewater
description: Waste water which was converted into an effluent that can be either returned to the water cycle with minimal environmental issues or reused.

label: desalinated water
description: Saline water from which minerals have been removed to produce fresh water suitable for human consumption or irrigation.

label: loamy sand
description: Soil which is primarily composed of sand with silt and clay in progressively smaller proportions.

Some authorities consider this a soil type, composed of 70-86% of sand, 0-30% of silt and 0-15% of clay. Others consider this a soil material that contains at the upper limit 85 to 90% sand, and the percentage of silt plus 1.5 times the percentage of clay is not less than 15, at the lower limit it contains not less than 70 to 85% sand, and the percentage of silt plus twice the percentage of clay does not exceed 30.

label: fine sand
description: Sand which is composed primarily of fine particles.
Thresholds for what particle size is considered "fine" vary by region and authority, as well as the tolerance for proportions of other particle sizes.

label: sandy loam
description: Loam which has a high proportion of sand in its composition.

Some authorities consider sandy loam to be a soil composed of 50-70% sand, 0-50% silt, and 0-20% clay. Others, a soil material that contains either 20% or less clay, with a percentage of silt plus twice the percentage of clay that exceeds 30, and 52% or more sand; or less than 7% clay, less than 50% silt, and between 43% and 52% sand.

label: silty loam
description: Loam which has a high proportion of silt in its composition.
Some authorities consider silt loam to be a soil composed of 20-50% of sand, 74-88% silt and 0-27% of clay.

label: sandy clay loam
description: Clay loam which has a high proportion of sand in its composition.
Some authorities consider sandy clay loam to be a soil composed of 45-80% sand, 0-28% silt, and 20-35% clay.

label: clay loam
description: Loam which has a high proportion of clay in its composition.
Some authorities consider clay loam to be a soil composed of 20-45% sand, 15-52% silt, and 27 to 40% clay.

label: silty clay loam
description: Clay loam which has a high proportion of silt in its composition.
Some authorities consider silty clay loam to be a soil composed of 0-20% of sand, 40-73 of silt and 27-40% of clay.

label: sandy clay
description: Clay which has a high proportion of sand in its composition.

Some authorities consider sandy clay to be a soil composed of 45-65% of sand, 0-20% of silt and 35-55% of clay. If the proportion of sand exceeds that of clay, it is unclear whether this is still considered clay (due to other properties) or whether a new class "clay sand" should be created.

label: silty clay
description: Clay which has a high proportion of silt in its composition.

Some authorities consider this a soil composed of 0-20% of sand, 40-60% of silt and 40-60% of clay. If the proportion of silt exceeds that of clay, it is unclear whether this is still considered clay (due to other properties) or whether a new class "clay silt" should be created.

label: marine mucilage
description: The formation of marine mucilage is often associated with conditions which stress marine microorganisms such as diatoms.
A gelatinous material primarily composed of exopolymeric compounds with colloidal properties, formed through the aggregation of marine snow particles, often found in large sheets,  flocs, and clouds.

label: biochar
description: charcoal that is used as a soil amendment.

label: lignite
description: It is considered the lowest rank of coal due to its relatively low heat content. It has a carbon content around 60–70 percent.
A soft, brown, combustible, sedimentary rock formed from naturally compressed peat.

label: bitumous coal
description: a relatively soft coal containing a tarlike substance called bitumen or asphalt. It is of higher quality than lignite coal but of poorer quality than anthracite. It is an organic sedimentary rock formed by diagenetic and sub metamorphic compression of peat bog material.

label: anthracite
description: A hard, compact variety of coal that has a submetallic luster. It has the highest carbon content, the fewest impurities, and the highest energy density of all types of coal and is the highest ranking of coal.

label: coke
description: Coal heated in the absence of air.

label: food product
description: Food material for humans and animals which is processed with the intention that it be consumable as a whole or added to other food products.

The FoodOn "food product" class is provided as a branch under which new food product categories and food products themselves can be placed. Here classes are provided to differentiate a food product by its food composition, processing and/or consumption characteristics. This avoids brand name products but it may include generic food dish categories. It has a much greater depth and polyhierarchy than other agency product type schemes have in an effort to group related products together.  The upper level basis of this tree originated in the environment ontology (ENVO) and from the US Code of Federal Regulations.

label: fermented agave juice
description: The juice products which are made from the fermented sap of the maguey (agave) plant.

label: fermenting sugar cane juice
description: This food product type includes food products which are made from fermentation of juice extracted from pressed sugarcane.

label: fermenting elaeis palm sap food product
mammalian meat food product
description: A food product made of meat, the skeletal muscle and associated fat, and other edible tissues such as organs, livers, skin, brains, bone marrow, kidneys, or lungs, of mammals.

label: meat sausage food product
description: A processed meat food product that is made from a sausage.

label: liver paste
description:

label: hot dog
description: A hot dog is a moist sausage of soft, even texture and flavor, often made from advanced meat recovery or meat slurry. Most types are fully cooked, cured or smoked. It is often placed hot in a special purpose soft, sliced hot dog bun.

label: processed meat food product
description: A processed food product consisting of meat which has been subjected to preservation and/or taste altering processes such as grinding, salting, curing, fermentation, smoking, and addition of chemical preservatives.

label: cheese food product
description: Cheese is a food derived from milk that is produced in a wide range of flavors, textures, and forms by coagulation of the milk protein casein.

label: yogurt food product
description: A dairy product produced by bacterial fermentation of milk.

The bacteria used to make yogurt are known as yogurt cultures. The fermentation of lactose by these bacteria produces lactic acid, which acts on milk protein to give yogurt its texture and characteristic tart flavor.

label: plant food product
description: This class includes food products which are derived from or produced by a plant.

label: cabbage food product
description: Cabbage or headed cabbage (comprising several cultivars of Brassica oleracea) is a leafy green or purple biennial plant, grown as an annual vegetable crop for its dense-leaved heads.

label: wort food product
description: The liquid extracted from the mashing process during the brewing of beer or whiskey. Wort contains the sugars that will be fermented by the brewing yeast to produce alcohol.

label: mammalian milk butter
description: Cream component produced by churning and containing not less than 80% milkfat.

label: Brie cheese food product
description: A large disc of smooth, soft, even runny cheese made with cow's milk.

label: gouda cheese food product
description: A hard cow's milk cheese with an almost orange yellow paste. Older cheeses are coated in black wax.

label: gorgonzola cheese food product
description: A drum of very rich, creamy, pungent blue-veined cow's milk cheese. It has a white paste with blue veining and a brined rind. It is made in Gorgonzola, near Milan.

label: swiss cheese food product
description: A generic cheese common to many countries for several related varieties of cheese  which resemble the Swiss Emmental. Three types of bacteria are used in the production of Emmental cheese: Streptococcus salivarius subsp. thermophilus, Lactobacillus  (L. helveticus or Lactobacillus delbrueckii subsp. bulgaricus), and Propionibacter (P. freudenreichii or P. shermani). In a late stage of cheese production, the Propionibacter consumes the lactic acid excreted by the other bacteria, and releases carbon dioxide gas, which slowly forms the bubbles that develop the eyes. Swiss cheese without eyes is known as "blind."

label: emmenthal cheese
description: A semi-hard, yellow cheese that has mild flavor that is slightly buttery.

label: new zealand cheddar cheese food product
pont ieveque cheese food product
description: A small, sweetish, soft, square cow's milk cheese from Normandy with a yellowish-orange rind.

label: vacherin mont dor cheese food product
description: A disc of soft cheese made with cow's milk. It has a soft to runny paste and a smooth, pink rind.

label: pork meat food product
description: A food product made from domestic pig meat (Sus domesticus or Sus scrofa scrofa).

label: cured meat food product
description: A meat that is preserved by the addition of a combination of salt, sugar, nitrates  or nitrite and or is smoked.

label: chicken meat food product
description: A food product that is derived from some chicken meat.

label: cow food product
description: A food product that is derived from some cow.

label: ice cream food product
description: A frozen dessert usually made from dairy products, such as milk and cream, and often combined with fruits or other ingredients and flavours. Most varieties contain sugar, although some are made with other sweeteners. In some cases, artificial flavourings  and colourings are used in addition to (or in replacement of) the natural ingredients. This mixture is stirred slowly while cooling to prevent large ice crystals from forming; the result is a smoothly textured ice cream.

label: animal seafood product
description: A seafood product is a vertebrate or invertibrate organism from an aquatic environment.

label: pork chop food product
description: A cut of meat (a meat chop) cut perpendicularly to the spine of the pig and usually containing a rib or part of a vertebra, served as an individual portion.

label: tempeh food product
description: A food product having tempeh as a defining ingredient

label: fermented fish or seafood food product
flour food product

description: Cheese made from milk or milk components, such as cream, by the following process: (1) produce curd through coagulation of milk by bacterial action and/or enzymes and/or acidification and draining of whey. (2) For cured cheese only: cure the curd. Excludes products made through further processing, such as comminuting (see *CHEESE PRODUCT*).

label: confectionery (us cfr)
description: Candy or other food product made with sweeteners and frequently containing nuts, fruits, starches, flavorings and other foods (21 CFR 170.3(n)(9). [FDA CFSAN 1995]

label: candy (us cfr)
description: Food product prepared by heating a mixture of sweeteners and other optional ingredients according to the specific formula for each subgroup.

label: fruit jelly (us cfr)
description: Jelled product made from one or more fruit juices and optional ingredients. Includes both fruit jelly, which may be sweetened with nutritive carbohydrate sweeteners, (21 CFR 150.140), and artificially sweetened fruit jelly (21 CFR 150.141). The finished fruit jelly must have a soluble solid content of no less than 65% and the ratio by weight of the fruit ingredient to sweetener in the starting mixture must be no less than 45:55. Artificially sweetened fruit jelly must contain no less than 55% fruit ingredient by weight.

label: fudge (us cfr)
description: Soft candy prepared by boiling milk, sugar, salt and optional ingredients to the soft-ball stage (238 degrees F.).

label: margarine (us cfr)
description: Food product having functional characteristics similar to those of butter; it is in plastic form or liquid emulsion and contains not less than 80% fat whose origin is vegetable or rendered animal carcass fats or a mixture of these as well as other optional ingredients specified by 21 CFR 166.110.

label: fruit or vegetable product (us cfr)
description: Fruits and vegetables in all forms. [FDA CFSAN 1995]

label: USA agency food product type
description: Food group having common consumption, functional or manufacturing characteristics, e.g. *FRUIT OR VEGETABLE PRODUCT*, *DAIRY PRODUCT*, *CONFECTIONARY*, *PREPARED FOOD PRODUCT*, etc. [FDA CFSAN 1995]

label: soft candy (us cfr)
description: Candy prepared by cooking a mixture of water, sugars and optional ingredients to a temperature of 250 degrees F. or less.

label: butter product analog (us cfr)
description: A food product having functional characteristics similar to a butter product; it may be nutritionally equivalent or inferior to the product it purports to resemble.

description: LanguaL curation note: This term is for CLASSIFICATION ONLY; DO NOT USE term in indexing. Use a more precise narrower term.

label: agency food product type
description: An agency food product type is a class of food product defined by an agency or consortium.

This class is designed to hold 3rd party food classification schemes which are being mapped to FoodOn classes using the 'has member' relation. The two hierarchies are not melded into a subclass polyhierarchy because of possible logical inconsistencies in the agency schemes. The hierarchies of agency schemes are as true to their agency representation as possible.

label: Codex Alimentarius classification of food and feed commodities
description:
Codex Alimentarius, Volume 2 - 1993, Section 2:  Pesticide Residues in Food.

The Codex Classification of food and animal feed commodities moving in trade and the description of the various items and groups of food and animal feedstuffs included in the present document have been developed by the Codex Committee on Pesticide Residues. It was first adopted by the 18th Session of the Codex Alimentarius Commission, (1989).

The Codex Classification includes food commodities and animal feedstuffs for which Codex maximum residue limits will not necessarily be established. The Classification is intended to be as complete a listing of food commodities in trade as possible, classified into groups on the basis of the commodity's similar potential for pesticide residues.

The Classification may also be appropriate for other purposes such as setting maximum levels for other types of residues or for other contaminants in food. The Codex Classification should be consulted in order to obtain a precise description of the food or animal feed commodities and, especially, in cases where Codex maximum residue limits have been set for groups of food and groups of animal feedstuffs. The Codex Classification is intended to promote harmonization of the terms used to describe commodities which are subject to maximum residue limits and of the approach to grouping commodities with similar potential for residue for which a common group maximum residue limit can be set.
LanguaL curation note: This term is for CLASSIFICATION ONLY; DO NOT USE term in indexing. Use a more precise narrower term.

label: a.  primary food commodities of plant origin (ccpr)
description: LanguaL curation note: This term is for CLASSIFICATION ONLY; DO NOT USE term in indexing. Use a more precise narrower term.

label: 02  vegetables (ccpr)
description:
Vegetables are foods derived from many different kinds of plants mostly annual and usually cultivated, commonly known by custom and tradition as "vegetables".
In several countries, some of these commodities grown on large areas are distinguished as "field crops" or arable crops e.g. sugar beet. For the sake of convenience in this guide such crops are classified under Type 2 Vegetables.
Exposure to pesticides is dependent on the particular part of the plant used for food and the growing practices.
Vegetables may be consumed in whole or in part and in the form of fresh, dried or processed foods.

label: 015  pulses (vd) (ccpr)
description:
Pulses are derived from the mature seeds naturally or artificially dried, of leguminous plants known as beans (dry) and peas (dry).
The seeds in the pods are protected from most pesticides applied during the growing season except pesticides which show a systemic action. The dried beans and peas however are often exposed to post-harvest treatments.
The dry pulses are consumed after processing or household cooking.

label: eurofir food classification
description: LanguaL curation note: This term is for CLASSIFICATION ONLY; DO NOT USE term in indexing. Use a more precise narrower term.

label: seafood or related product (eurofir)
description: The group includes marine or freshwater fish, molluscs, crustaceans, and other fauna such as reptiles, insects or frogs not in the Meats group. The group also includes seafood product analogs and seafood-based sausage or luncheon meat as well as such products as squid ink and clam juice.

label: seafood product (eurofir)
description: Includes fish offal; a food product whose predominant constituent is fish (e.g. dried and salted fish, smoked fish, canned fish, pickled fish, restructured fish and fish analogues, surimi; fish paste, pâté).

label: beverage (non-milk) (eurofir)
description: Alcoholic or non-alcoholic beverage; excludes milk and milk-based beverages.

label: non alcoholic beverage (eurofir)
description: Beverage containing no more than 0.5% alcohol; it may be flavoured, sweetened or carbonated; includes soft drinks and steeped beverages; excludes milk in all forms, fruit juices and vegetable juices.

label: coffee, tea, cocoa or infusion (eurofir)
description: Beverage prepared by extracting flavour and other components from food sources by percolation and/or immersion in water, usually at near-boiling temperature. The group includes coffee (e.g. instant coffee, coffee and chicory essence), tea, herbal tea (e.g. green tea, black tea, tisane), cocoa beverage and beverage powder.
LanguaL curation note: Renamed from *COFFEE, TEA, COCOA (EUROFIR)* (LanguaL 2010).

label: miscellaneous food product (eurofir)
description: EFG group 32, Eurocode-2 group 12.
LanguaL curation note: Use for foods and ingredients that could not fit into any of the above classes.

label: prepared food product (eurofir)
description: This subgroup includes multicomponent meals, sauces, retail salads, desserts, soups, snacks and other foods where similarity of the product type is more significant than the source of the principal ingredient(s).
synonyms: soup, sauce or miscellaneous food product

label: soup (eurofir)
description: A liquid food made by simmering meat, poultry, seafood or vegetables, being clear or thickened to the consistency of a thin puree or having milk or cream added, and often containing pieces of solid food such as meat, shellfish, pasta or vegetables. Soup takes precedence over other food products. Examples are egg and lemon soup, oxtail soup, fish soup, rice soup, lentil soup, minestrone, cherry soup.

label: GS1 Global Product Classification (GPC)
description:
The Global System 1 (GS1) Global Product Classification (GPC) is a system that gives buyers and sellers a common language for grouping products in the same way, everywhere in the world.$br/$
The GS1 GPC classification in facet A is currently updated based on June 2017 release of GS1 GPC Standard for Food/Beverage/Tobacco, except for codes pertaining to tobacco. See the GS1 site for details [https://www.gs1.org/standards/gpc].

label: U.S. code of federal regulations, title 21 food product type

label: sugar
description: A broad term that includes the nutritive sweeteners dextrose, fructose, galactose, lactose, maltose and sucrose, which are simple carbohydrates with molecules composed of one or two saccharide units. Note that on a product label or in a recipe, 'sugar' means *SUCROSE* and should be so indexed. Use the broad term *SUGAR* only if the specific sugar used is not known or not listed in the vocabulary.

label: food material by organism
description: Food material which is distinguished primarily by the organism(s) it derives from.

LanguaL curation note: "e.g. *LEAF*, *ROOT OR TUBER*, *ORGAN MEAT*, *MILK* OR *EGG*; it also includes components of parts, such as *CREAM*, and extracts, concentrates or isolates, such as *PROTEIN EXTRACT* or *SUGAR*."
Old definition as of Feb 25, 2025: Anatomical or other part(s) or substances derived from plant or animal or fungal organisms.

label: carbohydrate extract, concentrate, or isolate
description: Extract, concentrate or isolate high in sugar, oligosaccharide or polysaccharide.

label: brown sugar
description: Soft sugar whose crystals are covered by a film of refined dark syrup that imparts color, flavor, and moisture.

label: animal material
description: Langual note: Includes eggs and milk that, although separated from the animal, are produced as integral parts and are affected by the animal's food intake and metabolism.
Material that derives from some animal.
This branch isn't necessarily food material

label: extract, concentrate or isolate of plant or animal
description: A physical-chemical component separated from the food source or its parts by extraction, centrifugation, filtration, heat processing, expressing or a similar process. The separated component may be converted through further processing. If this is done, the final substance is indexed. A water-extracted component may remain in aqueous dispersion. The extract, concentrate or isolate is indexed in preference to the anatomic part from which it is derived. For example, peanut oil is indexed under *PEANUT* combined wih *FAT OR OIL* rather than with *SEED OR KERNEL*. On the other hand, fruit and vegetable juices can be indexed under *FRUIT JUICE OR NECTAR* or *VEGETABLE JUICE* (A. PRODUCT TYPE); therefore the anatomic part of the plant should be indexed.

label: mammalian milk whey
description: The serum or watery part of milk that is separated from the thicker or more coagulable part or curd, espcially in the process of making cheese; it contains lactose, minerals and lactalbumin.

label: seed oil
description: The oil produced by pressing or extracting lipids from plant seeds (e.g. grapeseed oil, rapeseed oil, linseed oil) /AM

label: food (liquid, low viscosity)
description: A liquid that flows very easily at room temperature.

Examples are: water, apple juice, sherry, acidophilus milk, whipping cream and some heavy liqueurs. The range of low viscosity liquid spans sucrose solutions between 0 and 45% solids (viscosity range from 1 to 10 centipoise). Prefer 'solid pieces' factor term to 'small particles' if both appear in the food.

label: food (liquid)
description: A state of matter between a solid and a gas, in which a substance has the capacity to flow and conforms to the shape of the container.

Liquids range from water to honey, corresponding to a range in viscosity (or apparent viscosity) from 1 to 500 centipoise (viscosity is a measure of a liquid's resistance to flow). Products that are pourable but have a higher viscosity are *SEMILIQUID*.

description: LanguaL curation note: With the exception of peanut (see *PEANUT OR PEANUT BUTTER ADDED*), used when a nut or seed ingredient is the second ingredient in order of predominance.
